_note: The organism pack (app/organism_pack.py): every species as an animal (from biology, dossiers, the food webs, the habitat engine and the games' encounter times), the Gen IV characteristics and each nature's flavours, each game's TMs and HMs and who can be taught them (machines[vg].have[species id]: a hex digit per four machines, bit i%4 of digit i//4), the type chart and defensive abilities (rules.py's, for exposure), and the organism rules. Reference only.

rules._note: The organism (v2.8, docs/ORGANISM.md): how Blackthorn reads a Pokémon as a living animal in the wild, species first and then the individual. Every block says its class: mechanic (the games' own data or rules), inferred (Blackthorn's reading of game data: types, body shapes, abilities read as biology), canon (the Pokédex, quoted) or creative. biology/organism.py and its browser copy (app/web/44_organism.html) only evaluate them; app/test_organism_parity.mjs holds the two together. Ability traits also reach the capability engine as plausible evidence (capability/model.json → ability_traits, read from here by app/capability_pack.py).

exposure._note: How a place's conditions treat a body, read from the type chart (the type that attacks a body in those conditions, against its types and ability): super effective is hard on it, resisted means it's at home. A hard condition is eased by the team capability named here; without it the day is hard going for that member (a strain, never a setback).

dossier.summary: Venusaur is a 2 m, 100 kg grassland quadruped carrying a large flower on its back, and it runs partly on sunlight: the spread petals catch the sun's rays and fill its body with power, so it is strongest in summer and keeps moving to find sun. Its flower gives off a fragrance that soothes people and calms animals in the middle of a fight, strongest after rain, and the scent draws other Pokémon to it. The line begins as Bulbasaur, which hatches with a seed on its back and lives off the seed's stored nutrients while it is young. No Gen I–IV game has the line in the wild; every Venusaur is raised from a starter Bulbasaur.

dossier.summary: Charizard is a winged, fire-breathing mountain Pokémon: 1.7 m and 90.5 kg, able to fly to nearly 4,600 feet and breathe fire hot enough to melt boulders. It flies about looking for strong opponents and never turns its fire on one weaker than itself, though its flames can start forest fires by accident. Its tail flame, which in Charmander is a measure of its life, flares whitish-blue when it is furious. Every Charizard in Gen I–IV is raised from a Charmander given to a trainer; the line's wild home is described only as the rocky mountains where Charmeleon's tails shine at night like stars.
diet: Charmander prefers hot places and hot things, but that is a preference for heat, not a diet; the machine reading's 'thermotroph' came from its Fire type alone.
senses: Charmander's tail flame makes a sound as it burns, audible only in quiet places; whether the adult's is louder is not recorded.
behavior: It flies about in search of strong opponents.

defense: Its breath inflicts terrible pain on enemies.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: mountain. Charmeleon live in rocky mountains, where their fiery tails shine at night like stars.

dossier.summary: Blastoise is a heavy, shelled water's-edge Pokémon (1.6 m, 85.5 kg) that carries pressurised water jets on its shell. It plants its feet before firing, and makes itself heavy on purpose to take the recoil; the jets hit harder than a fire hose, can punch through thick steel, and are accurate enough to knock a can over from 160 feet. In a pinch it withdraws into its shell or crushes an attacker under its weight. The line hunts from the water: Squirtle shoots water at prey and Wartortle hides in water to stalk it, and old Wartortle are known by the algae on their shells. No game in Gen I–IV has the line in the wild; every one is raised from a starter Squirtle.
diet: A predator in its early stages: Squirtle shoots water at prey while in the water, and Wartortle hides in water to stalk unwary prey.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Hitting a can at 160 feet implies good eyesight and fine aim.

social: The scratches on Wartortle's shell are evidence of its toughness as a fighter, which implies frequent fights, with rivals or predators.
defense: In a pinch it withdraws inside its shell; otherwise it crushes its foe under its heavy body.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: the water's edge.

dossier.summary: The leaf-eating larva of Butterfree. Caterpie climbs trees on sticky feet, eats leaves bigger than itself, hides among foliage of its own green, and when its red feeler is touched it releases a foul smell. It grows by moulting several times, then covers itself in silk and becomes Metapod. In HeartGold it is the animal most often met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day, and it is never met there at night; in SoulSilver, Weedle takes its place slot for slot.
diet: It eats leaves, voraciously: it can eat a leaf bigger than its own body while you watch.

dossier.summary: The pupa of the Butterfree line: a hardened green shell, nearly motionless, inside which Caterpie's body is rebuilt into Butterfree. It doesn't eat and can do little but harden its shell further; the body inside is soft and tender, and a large enough knock can pop it out of the shell. Its whole strategy is to stay still, armoured and out of the way. In HeartGold it is met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day and in the common Headbutt trees, a stage that lasts, in the games, from level 7 to level 10.

In SoulSilver it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest.

dossier.summary: The adult of the Caterpie line, and the only member of the Ilex Forest community whose entries describe it visiting flowers. Butterfree flies from flower to flower collecting honey, which it rubs onto the hairs of its legs and carries back to a nest; it can find flowers in bloom a long way off, by some entries more than six miles. A powder on its wings sheds rain, so it forages even in the heaviest downpours, and in a fight the same dust is toxic. In HeartGold it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees.

senses: It can identify flowers in bloom at a distance, has a superior ability to search out honey, and can locate flower patches with only tiny amounts of pollen.
behavior: It collects honey every day and in all weather: its water-repellent wings let it fly and forage even in the heaviest rain.

habitat: A forest animal by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold it is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees (10%), Route 47's secret Headbutt trees, National Park's Bug-Catching Contest, and in Kanto on Route 2 and in Viridian Forest. In SoulSilver it appears only in the Contest, and Beedrill holds its Ilex Forest slot.

Weedle carries a two-inch poison barb on its head and a bright body that warns enemies off; it hides in grass and bushes and under the leaves it eats, and it eats its own weight in leaves every day. A keen sense of smell, through a big red nose, lets it tell the leaves it likes from those it doesn't. In Ilex Forest it is met in the morning and by day, never at night.

dossier.summary: The pupa of the Beedrill line. Kakuna clings to or leans against stout trees, or hides under leaves and in the angles of branches, almost unable to move while its body is remade inside a hardening shell. It is not defenceless: it can move a little and push out a poison barb if attacked. The shell grows hot to the touch from the work going on inside. In SoulSilver it is met in Ilex Forest's grass in the morning and by day and in the common Headbutt trees.

dossier.summary: The adult of the Weedle line: a large, fast, venomous insect with three poison stingers, one on each foreleg and the strongest on its tail. Beedrill is a hunter. It stings prey into submission and carries it back to its nest, defends that nest fiercely, and may attack in swarms; its favourite attack is a fast pass, striking with its needles and flying off. In SoulSilver it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees, in the slot Butterfree fills in HeartGold, which swaps the forest's flower-visitor for a predator.

dossier.summary: The small, docile ground bird of every forest edge and grassy route. Pidgey hides in tall grass, forages for small bugs, and has a clever trick: it flaps its wings rapidly in the grass to raise a dust cloud that drives insect prey into the open. The same dust is its defence; it would rather kick up blinding sand than fight, though if disturbed it can strike back ferociously. It has an extremely sharp sense of direction and finds its way home to its nest from however far away. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is one of the commonest daytime birds of Johto and Kanto, Viridian Forest among them.

dossier.summary: A territorial raptor of forest and grass. Pidgeotto claims a large territory and patrols it, flying slow circles with a sharp lookout; its vision is so good that however high it flies it can see its prey move. It downs prey with well-developed claws and carries it more than 60 miles to its nest, an Exeggcute for example, and it shows no mercy to anything that violates its territory. It is the one named predator of Magikarp, which it catches mid-jump. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it hunts by day on Routes 37 and 43 in Johto and Routes 2, 8, 13, 14, 15 and 25 and Viridian Forest in Kanto.

dossier.summary: A tiny, fierce bird of grassy places that eats bugs: it flaps its short wings to flush insects out of tall grass and plucks them with its stubby beak. Spearow is inept at flying high and must beat its short wings fast to stay up, but darts around at high speed to protect its territory, flying ceaselessly and crying. Its high, keening cry carries over half a mile, and when it echoes all around, the Spearow are warning each other of danger. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is one of the commonest birds in both regions: in the grass by day on Routes 33, 42, 46, 22, 3, 4, 7, 9 and 10, and shaken from the trees by Headbutt along most of Johto's mountain roads and in Kanto's towns.

eats: This intelligent Pokémon roasts hard Berries with electricity to make them tender enough to eat.

dossier.summary: A small forest mouse that stores electricity in pouches on its cheeks and uses it for almost everything. It lives in groups, monitors its surroundings with its tail raised, and when several gather their combined charge can build into a lightning storm. The Gold and HeartGold Pokédex call it intelligent enough to roast hard Berries with electricity until they are tender, and Ruby notes the blackened Berries left when it overdoes it. One Platinum entry has it recharging a weakened companion with a shock, and the young, Pichu, play at touching tails to set off sparks.
diet: It eats Berries, and roasts hard ones with electricity to make them tender enough to eat.
senses: The raised tail monitors its surroundings; what it detects is not said.
behavior: Vigilant: it keeps its tail raised to check its surroundings.
social: It lives in groups in the forest, and several together can build up enough electricity to cause lightning storms.
defense: Electric defence: threatened, it looses charges from its cheek sacs; angered, it discharges its stored energy at once.
habitat: A forest animal that lives with others of its kind; its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause paralysis.

about: When its electricity builds, its muscles are stimulated, and it becomes more aggressive than usual.
moves: If its electric pouches run empty, it raises its tail to gather electricity from the atmosphere.
defense: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high voltage power.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s evasion in a sandstorm.

about: If it fell from a great height, this Pokémon could save itself by rolling into a ball and bouncing.
eats: Burrows deep underground in arid locations far from water. It only emerges to hunt for prey.
defense: To protect itself from attackers, it curls up into a ball. It lives in arid regions with minimal rainfall.

dossier.summary: A small desert burrower with a very dry, extremely tough hide. Sandshrew lives in deep burrows in arid places far from water, which it dislikes, and its body absorbs water without waste. It only comes out to hunt. Its defence is a ball: it rolls itself instantly into one, and attacks bounce off it; rolled up, it could even survive a fall from a great height by bouncing. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's, in Union Cave and Mt. Moon, the dry inside of mountains rather than a desert.
diet: It only emerges to hunt for food, or for prey.
behavior: At night it burrows into the desert sand to sleep.
defense: It rolls itself instantly into a ball when threatened, and in a ball it makes any attack bounce off harmlessly.
habitat: Deep burrows in arid places far from water: it dislikes water and prefers dry, sandy places. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s evasion in a sandstorm.

about: In an attempt to hide itself, it will run around at top speed to kick up a blinding dust storm.
moves: In an attempt to hide itself, it will run around at top speed to kick up a blinding dust storm.
defense: If it digs at an incredible pace, it may snap off its spikes and claws. They grow back in a day.

dossier.summary: The spiny adult of Sandshrew. Sandslash's back is covered in tough spikes, hardened sections of its hide, which fall out once a year as new ones grow beneath; spikes and claws that snap off when it digs too fast grow back in a day. It curls into a spiny ball to protect itself, and to avoid heatstroke on hot days, and rolls into foes back first; in a fight it jabs with its spines to make the foe flinch, then leaps at it and tears with its claws. It climbs trees to attack from above, and kicks up a blinding dust storm to hide. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: Route 26, Route 27 and Mt. Moon.
diet: No entry says what Sandslash eats. Its young emerges only to hunt (27.10), so the line is a hunter.
behavior: It curls up to prevent heatstroke during the daytime when temperatures rise sharply.
defense: It curls up into a spiny ball when threatened, and can roll while curled up to attack or escape.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain; it is adept at climbing trees.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: The poison hidden in its small horn is extremely potent. Even a tiny scratch can have fatal results.
defense: The poison hidden in its small horn is extremely potent. Even a tiny scratch can have fatal results.

Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: When feeding its young, it first chews the food into a paste, then spits it out for the offspring.
eats: When feeding its young, it first chews the food into a paste, then spits it out for the offspring.
senses: When it senses danger, it raises all the barbs on its body. These barbs grow slower than Nidorino’s.
defense: It has a calm and caring nature. Because its horn grows slowly, it prefers not to fight.

dossier.summary: The female middle stage of the Nidoran line: a calm, caring, barbed animal that lives with friends and family. Nidorina keeps its barbs tucked away among its own so no one is hurt, raises them all at once when threatened, and grows nervous if separated from the others. It rests deep in a burrow, barbs retracted when relaxed, and feeds its young by chewing food into a paste and spitting it out for them. Its horn grows slowly, so it prefers not to fight. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Kanto's Routes 13, 14 and 15, beside the male Nidorino.
diet: When feeding its young, it first chews the food into a paste, then spits it out for the offspring.
senses: It senses danger, and raises its barbs when it does; how is not said. Its male counterpart raises its big ears to check its surroundings (33.3).
behavior: It has a calm and caring nature, a docile nature, a gentle temperament.
social: With friends or family, Nidorina keep their barbs tucked away to prevent hurting each other.
defense: If it is threatened with attack, or senses danger, it raises the barbs all over its body.
habitat: It rests deep in its burrow; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: Its body is covered with needle-like scales. It never shows signs of shrinking from any attack.
defense: It uses its scaly, rugged body to seal the entrance of its nest and protect its young from predators.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: It is small, but its horn is filled with poison. It charges then stabs with the horn to inject poison.
senses: It raises its big ears to check its surroundings. It will strike first if it senses any danger.
defense: It is small, but its horn is filled with poison. It charges then stabs with the horn to inject poison.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: It raises its big ears to check its surroundings. If it senses anything, it attacks immediately.
senses: It raises its big ears to check its surroundings. If it senses anything, it attacks immediately.
defense: Quick to anger, it stabs enemies with its horn to inject a powerful poison when it becomes agitated.

dossier.summary: The male middle stage of the Nidoran line, the young of the rival's Nidoking, and the female Nidorina's opposite in temper. Nidorino is aggressive, quick to anger and violent: it raises its big ears to check its surroundings and attacks the moment it senses anything, bristling every barb on its back and stabbing with a horn harder than a diamond that secretes a powerful venom on impact. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Kanto's Routes 13, 14 and 15, beside Nidorina.
diet: The machine reading's waste-eater comes from its Poison type alone. Its female counterpart chews food for its young (30.3) and its adult form breaks prey's bones (34.1), so the line is likely omnivorous or predatory, but nothing says which for Nidorino.
senses: Hearing: it raises its big ears to check its surroundings. Its young, Nidoran♂, can move its ears in any direction and misses not even the slightest sound (32.6).
behavior: An aggressive Pokémon that is quick to attack; easily agitated, easily angered, with a violent disposition.
social: Nothing is said about how Nidorino live. Rivalry, one of its abilities, makes it fiercer against foes of its own gender: males fight males, in game terms.
defense: If it senses a hostile presence, all the barbs on its back bristle up at once, and it challenges the foe with all its might.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; no entry describes where it lives.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Raises Attack if the foe is of the same gender.

about: It swings its big tail around during battle. If its foe flinches, it will charge with its sturdy body.
eats: It uses its powerful tail in battle to smash, constrict, then break the prey's bones.
defense: It is recognized by its rock-hard hide and its extended horn. Be careful with the horn as it contains venom.

dossier.summary: The adult male of the Nidoran line: a 1.4 m, 62 kg poison-horned, rock-hided brawler whose weapon is its tail. One swing can topple a metal transmission tower or snap a telephone pole like a matchstick, and the oldest entries say it uses the tail to smash, constrict and then break its prey's bones. Its horn is hard enough to pierce a diamond and contains venom. Once it goes on a rampage there is no stopping it. It is the rival's constant in Blackthorn's canon. Nidoking is never wild in a Gen I-IV game; it comes from a Nidorino given a Moon Stone, and Nidorino lives on Kanto's southern routes.
diet: It uses its powerful tail to smash, constrict, then break its prey's bones.
senses: Nothing is said about Nidoking's senses. Its young raise and turn their big ears to check their surroundings and miss even the slightest sound (32.6, 33.3), so hearing is the line's sense.
behavior: It swings its big tail around during battle; if its foe flinches, it charges with its sturdy body.
social: Nothing is said about how Nidoking live together. Rivalry, one of its abilities, makes it hit harder against foes of the same gender: in game terms, males fight males.
defense: A rock-hard hide and a venom horn; Poison Point poisons what touches it.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; no entry describes where it lives.

The Pokémon only takes damage from attacks.

about: The moonlight that it stores in the wings on its back apparently gives it the ability to float in midair.
senses: It is said that happiness will come to those who see a gathering of Clefairy dancing under a full moon.
moves: The moonlight that it stores in the wings on its back apparently gives it the ability to float in midair.

dossier.summary: A small, rare, moon-bound Pokémon of quiet mountains. Clefairy collects moonlight with the wings on its back, and the stored moonlight apparently lets it float in midair. It is rarely seen except on the night of a full moon, when groups come out to play; at dawn the tired Clefairy go back to their quiet mountain retreats and sleep nestled against each other. It is said that happiness comes to anyone who sees a gathering of Clefairy dancing under a full moon. Its cuteness makes it popular, even as a pet. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Mt. Moon, one encounter in twenty, in both versions.
diet: No entry says it eats food. It collects and stores moonlight, which gives it the power to float.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses; it responds to the full moon, so it senses moonlight.
behavior: On every night of a full moon, groups of Clefairy come out to play; when dawn arrives they return to their mountain retreats and sleep nestled against each other.
social: It lives with others: groups play together on full-moon nights and sleep nestled together.
defense: Rarity and retreat: it stays hidden in quiet mountains and comes out mostly on full-moon nights.
habitat: Quiet, deep mountains, where it is thought to live with others and where it sleeps; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause infatuation.
The Pokémon only takes damage from attacks.

about: With its acute hearing, it can pick up sounds from far away. It usually hides in quiet places.
senses: It is very wary and rarely shows itself to people. Its ears can hear a pin drop over half a mile away.
moves: A timid fairy Pokémon that is rarely seen. It will run and hide the moment it senses people.

abilities: It powers up Fire-type moves if it’s hit by one.

about: As it develops, its single white tail gains color and splits into six. It is quite warm and cuddly.
moves: It can freely control fire, making fiery orbs fly like will-o’-the-wisps. Just before evolution, its six tails grow hot as if on fire.

abilities: It powers up Fire-type moves if it’s hit by one.

about: Some legends claim that each of its nine tails has its own unique type of special mystical power.
senses: Ninetales casts a sinister light from its bright red eyes to gain total control over its foe’s mind. This Pokémon is said to live for a thousand years.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause infatuation.

about: If it inflates to SING a lullaby, it can perform longer and cause sure drowsiness in its audience.
senses: Looking into its cute, round eyes causes it to sing a relaxing melody, inducing its enemies to sleep.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause infatuation.

about: Their fur feels so good that if two of them snuggle together, they won't want to be separated.
senses: Their fur feels so good that if two of them snuggle together, they won't want to be separated.

about: While flying, it constantly emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth to check its surroundings.
senses: Even though it has no eyes, it can sense obstacles using ultrasonic waves it emits from its mouth.
moves: Emits ultrasonic cries while it flies. They act as a sonar used to check for objects in its way.

dossier.summary: An eyeless bat that finds its way by sound. Zubat flies through the dark sending ultrasonic cries from its mouth and reading their echoes to find obstacles and targets. It shuns sunlight, which burns it, and spends the day hanging upside down in colonies in caves, old buildings and deep forest. No Zubat entry says what it eats; its evolved form, Golbat, drinks blood. In Ilex Forest it is met mostly at night, and around Blackthorn it lives in the Ice Path and Dark Cave.
diet: Its evolved form drinks blood: Golbat punctures even tough hides with sharp fangs and gorges on the blood of people and Pokémon.
senses: Echolocation: it emits ultrasonic cries constantly as it flies and uses their reflections to check its surroundings, detect obstacles and fix its position.
behavior: Nocturnal: it stays unmoving in a dark spot through the bright daylight hours and sleeps until sundown.
social: Colonial: it forms colonies in perpetually dark places and gathers with others by day.
defense: No entry describes a defence. Its colonies, its dark roosts and flight are the obvious protections.
habitat: Dark places: caves, the ceilings of old buildings, the eaves of old houses, and deep forest.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from flinching.

about: However hard its victim's hide may be, it punctures with sharp fangs and gorges itself with blood.
eats: It can drink more than 10 ounces of blood at once. If it has too much, it gets heavy and flies clumsily.
moves: It can drink more than 10 ounces of blood at once. If it has too much, it gets heavy and flies clumsily.
defense: However hard its victim's hide may be, it punctures with sharp fangs and gorges itself with blood.

dossier.summary: The blood-drinking bat of the highland caves. Golbat's four fangs puncture even thick hide, it takes in more than ten ounces of blood at a time, and some entries say it will not stop feeding even when it is too heavy to fly. It hunts people and Pokémon at night, approaching unseen and striking from behind. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is common on every floor of the Ice Path and rare at the Blackthorn end of Dark Cave, which makes it the most likely predator of the warm-bodied animals in the Ice Path, though no entry names its prey.
diet: It drinks the blood of living things, people and Pokémon both.
senses: Zubat have no eyes and find their way by echolocation, emitting ultrasonic cries from the mouth.
behavior: Nocturnal: particularly active in the pitch black of night, and on inky, moonless nights.
social: Zubat form colonies in perpetually dark places and gather to hang from ceilings by day.
defense: Inner Focus (it can't be made to flinch), the Poison type, and a set of moves that disorient rather than wound: Supersonic, Confuse Ray (Lv 21), Mean Look (Lv 33), Haze (Lv 45).
habitat: In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on all four Ice Path floors (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F) at 30% at any time of day, Lv 22-23, and at the Blackthorn end of Dark Cave at 5% (Lv 23). Gold and Silver had the same 30% in the Ice Path; Crystal had more, 55-60% on 1F to B2F.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: Awakened by moonlight, it roams actively at night. In the day, it stays quietly underground.

dossier.summary: A walking weed. By day Oddish plants itself in fertile ground, face buried and only its leaves showing, and takes up nutrients from the soil through its whole body; at night moonlight wakes it, and it walks off on its root-feet, scattering seeds as it goes. It is Ilex Forest's night shift: in HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the animal most often met in the forest's grass after dark, and it is never met there by day. Pull one up and it shrieks.
diet: By day it buries itself in soil and absorbs nutrients from the ground through its entire body.
senses: It responds to moonlight: exposure to it starts it moving.
behavior: Nocturnal: moonlight wakes it, and it roams actively at night; by day it keeps its face buried and stays quietly underground. HeartGold and SoulSilver meet it in grass only at night.
defense: By day it buries itself with only its leaves showing, to avoid detection by its enemies, and it can be mistaken for a clump of weeds.
habitat: Grassland by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's grass at night (60%), on Routes 5, 6, 24 and 25 at night, and in the Johto Safari Zone at night.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.
eats: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.
senses: The smell from its drool-like syrup and the pollen on its petals is so bad, it may make opponents faint.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: It has the world's largest petals. With every step, the petals shake out heavy clouds of toxic pollen.
eats: Vileplume has the world’s largest petals. They are used to attract prey that are then doused with toxic spores. Once the prey are immobilized, this Pokémon catches and devours them.

abilities: Contact may paralyze, poison, or cause sleep.
Reduces HP if it is hot. Water restores HP.

about: It is doused with mushroom spores when it is born. As its body grows, mushrooms sprout from its back.

dossier.summary: A small bug that carries its own parasite. Paras burrows to suck and gnaw tree roots and draws juice from trunks, and the mushrooms on its back, called tochukaso, grow by taking nutrients from it; one entry says they take most of its food, another that they order the bug to feed. The spores reach it at birth, the mushrooms grow as it grows, and in Parasect the mushroom has taken over. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is met in Ilex Forest's grass at every hour, least often by day.
diet: It burrows to suck tree roots, or burrows under the ground to gnaw on them.
social: Nothing is said for Paras. As Parasect they infest large trees in numbers and move to another tree all at once, so the adults at least gather.
defense: Effect Spore: contact with it may paralyse, poison or put an attacker to sleep. Read biologically, the mushroom's spores defend the pair.
habitat: Forest, and underground among tree roots.

abilities: Contact may paralyze, poison, or cause sleep.
Reduces HP if it is hot. Water restores HP.

about: It stays mostly in dark, damp places, the preference not of the bug, but of the big mushroom on its back.

dossier.summary: A bug that has been taken over by the mushroom on its back. In Parasect the mushroom has grown larger than the bug's body and controls it: it drains the bug's energy and appears to do all the thinking, and it is the mushroom, not the bug, that prefers dark, damp places. Parasect infest the roots and lower trunks of large trees in numbers and drain their nutrients, all moving to a new tree when one dies. When there is nothing left to take from the bug, the mushrooms leave spores on the bug's egg. Its spores are toxic, and used as herbal medicine. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Cerulean Cave, one encounter in four.
diet: Parasect infest large trees en masse and drain nutrients from the lower trunk and roots.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses; the mushroom 'appears to do all the thinking'.
behavior: When an infested tree dies, they move onto another tree all at once.
social: They infest trees en masse and move together, so Parasect live in groups on a shared host tree.
defense: It scatters toxic, poisonous spores from the mushroom cap; the larger the mushroom grows, the stronger the spores.
habitat: It stays mostly in dark, damp places, the preference not of the bug but of the big mushroom on its back.

about: Its eyes also function as radar units. It catches and eats small bugs that hide in darkness.
eats: Its eyes also function as radar units. It catches and eats small bugs that hide in darkness.
senses: Its eyes also function as radar units. It catches and eats small bugs that hide in darkness.
defense: Poison oozes from all over its body. It catches and eats small bugs at night that are attracted by light.

abilities: Blocks the added effects of attacks taken.

about: When it attacks, it flaps its large wings violently to scatter its poisonous powder all around.
eats: Venomoth are nocturnal--they only are active at night. Their favorite prey are insects that gather around streetlights, attracted by the light in the darkness.
defense: The dustlike scales covering its wings are color-coded to indicate the kinds of poison it has.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s evasion in a sandstorm.

about: Its skin is very thin. If it is exposed to light, its blood heats up, causing it to grow weak.
eats: Lives about one yard underground where it feeds on plant roots. It sometimes appears aboveground.
moves: If a Diglett DIGS through a field, it leaves the soil perfectly tilled and ideal for planting crops.

dossier.summary: A tiny mole that lives about a yard underground, feeding on plant and tree roots. Diglett's skin is very thin: in light its blood heats up and it grows weak, so it prefers dark places and sticks its head out only when the sun isn't bright. It burrows at a shallow depth, leaving raised earth in its wake, and wherever it digs through a field it leaves the soil perfectly tilled for planting, which is why Diglett are raised on most farms. Its tunnels are sometimes Onix's, which Diglett use as homes. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it fills Diglett's Cave, the tunnel Diglett dug from Route 2 to Route 11 by Vermilion City, and is found on Route 48 and under the rocks of Vermilion.
diet: It feeds on plant roots, about one yard underground, and chews on tree roots.
senses: Its thin skin reacts to light: light heats its blood. That is the one sense-like thing the entries give it.
behavior: It spends most of its time underground; it sometimes appears above ground, sticking its head out only when the sun isn't bright.
social: Nothing is said about Diglett living together. Diglett's Cave holds them nine in ten, so they live densely where they live.
defense: It stays underground, out of reach.
habitat: Underground, about a yard down, at a shallow depth; it prefers dark places and may pop up in caves. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s evasion in a sandstorm.

about: Its three heads bob separately up and down to loosen the soil nearby, making it easier for it to burrow.
moves: Extremely powerful, they can DIG through even the hardest ground to a depth of over 60 miles.

dossier.summary: Diglett triplets that emerged from one body, so each thinks exactly like the other two, and they work together to burrow endlessly. Dugtrio's three heads bob up and down separately to loosen the soil, driving it through the hardest ground to depths of over 60 miles; its burrowing triggers huge earthquakes, and some people mistake its passing for one. In battle it digs through the ground and strikes from an unexpected direction. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only in Diglett's Cave, one encounter in ten, among the Diglett.
diet: It is three Diglett, which feed on plant and tree roots (50.1, 50.5); it most likely does too.
behavior: Extremely powerful, it digs through even the hardest ground, and can burrow at over 60 mph.
social: Because the triplets split from one body, each thinks exactly like the other two.
defense: In battle it digs through the ground and strikes the unsuspecting foe from an unexpected direction.
habitat: Underground, through even the hardest ground, to depths of over 60 miles; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: The Pokémon may pick up items.
Powers up the Pokémon’s weaker moves.

about: It is fascinated by round objects. It can't stop playing with them until it tires and falls asleep.
senses: It is nocturnal in nature. If it spots something shiny, its eyes glitter brightly.
defense: Meowth withdraw their sharp claws into their paws to silently sneak about. For some reason, this Pokémon loves shiny coins that glitter with light.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from paralysis.
Powers up the Pokémon’s weaker moves.

about: Many adore it for its sophisticated air. However, it will lash out and scratch for little reason.
eats: Behind its lithe, elegant appearance lies a barbaric side. It will tear apart its prey on a mere whim.
senses: A Persian’s six bold whiskers sense air movements to determine what is in its vicinity. It becomes docile if grabbed by the whiskers.

about: It has mystical powers but doesn't recall that it has used them. That is why it always looks puzzled.

dossier.summary: A pond duck with a constant headache and powers it can't remember using. When the headache peaks, Psyduck shows psychic or telekinetic power, apparently in an altered state like deep sleep, and afterwards it has no memory of it, which is why it always looks puzzled. Not one entry says what it eats or where it lives. HeartGold and SoulSilver put it on the water: it is 90% of what is met surfing Ilex Forest's pond.
diet: Its moves suggest a scratching, splashing forager (Scratch at Lv 1, Water Gun 9, Fury Swipes 27), and a duck at the water's edge suggests water plants and small animals; but that is a guess from its body plan.
behavior: It is constantly tormented by headaches, and when a headache peaks or worsens it starts using strange powers.
defense: It lulls enemies with its vacant look while it uses psychokinetic powers: a 'wily' animal, in the oldest entry.
habitat: Water's edge by Gen 3 habitat. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is surfed on Ilex Forest's pond (90%), Route 35 and Route 6, walks in Seafoam Islands, surfs in Cerulean Cave, and is in the Johto Safari Zone.

about: When it swims at full speed using its long, webbed limbs, its forehead somehow begins to glow.
moves: When it swims at full speed using its long, webbed limbs, its forehead somehow begins to glow.

dossier.summary: The adult of Psyduck, and the strongest swimmer in the Ilex Forest community. Golduck has long limbs ending in webbed flippers and a streamlined body; the entries call it the fastest swimmer among Pokémon, faster than any human champion, and it copes with rough seas as well as the quiet lakes and slow rivers it prefers. It appears by waterways at dusk, and its forehead glows when it swims flat out or uses its psychic power. People have mistaken it for the kappa, and it has rescued sailors from wrecks. In Ilex Forest it is the rarer of the pond's two surfing encounters (10%).
diet: Its speed suggests a pursuit hunter, and the pond's fish make the obvious prey: Magikarp (0.9 m, 10.0 kg) and Poliwag (0.6 m, 12.4 kg) share its water and are far smaller.
behavior: It swims elegantly, gracefully and dynamically, using its limbs and flippers.
defense: No entry describes a defence; speed in the water is the obvious one.
habitat: Lakes and lakeshores, and the quiet, slow-moving rivers it is fond of; it also swims easily in rough, stormy seas.

Raises Attack upon taking a critical hit.

about: It is extremely ill-tempered. Groups of them will attack any handy target for no reason.
senses: It lives in groups in the treetops. If it loses sight of its group, it becomes infuriated by its loneliness.
moves: Light and agile on its feet, and ferocious in temperament. When angered, it flies into an uncontrollable frenzy.

about: If approached while asleep, it may awaken and angrily give chase in a groggy state of semi-sleep.
senses: It becomes wildly furious if it even senses someone looking at it. It chases anyone that meets its glare.
moves: It grows angry if you see its eyes and gets angrier if you run. If you beat it, it gets even madder.

abilities: It powers up Fire-type moves if it’s hit by one.

about: It has a brave and trustworthy nature. It fearlessly stands up to bigger and stronger foes.
senses: It controls a big territory. If it detects an unknown smell, it roars loudly to force out the intruder.
defense: Extremely loyal, it will fearlessly bark at any opponent to protect its own trainer from harm.

abilities: It powers up Fire-type moves if it’s hit by one.

about: This legendary Chinese Pokémon is considered magnificent. Many people are enchanted by its grand mane.
senses: Its magnificent bark conveys a sense of majesty. Anyone hearing it can't help but grovel before it.
moves: This fleet-footed Pokémon is said to run over 6,200 miles in a single day and night. The fire that blazes wildly within its body is its source of power.

dossier.summary: Arcanine is a big, fast, fire-powered quadruped (1.9 m, 155 kg) of open grassland, admired since ancient times for its beauty, its grand mane and the way it runs, 'agilely as if on wings'. The fire blazing inside its body is its source of power, and its bark carries such majesty that anyone who hears it grovels. Much of what is written about it is legend: Chinese stories, and a claim that it can run over 6,200 miles in a day and night. It develops from Growlithe, a brave, loyal and fiercely territorial animal with a nose that never forgets a scent and can read the emotions of others. Arcanine forms only when a Growlithe is exposed to a Fire Stone, and none is wild in Gen I–IV.
diet: Its wild moves are mostly bites (Bite, Fire Fang, Thunder Fang, and Crunch for Growlithe), which suggests a meat-eater, but that is a reading of moves.
senses: Growlithe has a superb sense of smell and never forgets a scent.
behavior: A runner: speed is the thing it is most known for.
social: Growlithe is friendly, brave and trustworthy, and stands up fearlessly to bigger, stronger foes.
defense: Intimidation first: Intimidate lowers an opponent's attack, Roar (Lv 1) drives it off, and the canon bark makes listeners grovel.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: grassland. An ancient picture scroll shows it running through prairies.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by a Water-type move.

about: Because it is inept at walking on its newly grown legs, it always swims around in water.
eats: The swirl on its belly is its insides showing through the skin. It looks clearer after it eats.
senses: It is possible to see this Pokémon’s spiral innards right through its thin skin. However, the skin is also very flexible. Even sharp fangs bounce right off it.
moves: Because it is inept at walking on its newly grown legs, it always swims around in water.
defense: It is possible to see this Pokémon’s spiral innards right through its thin skin. However, the skin is also very flexible. Even sharp fangs bounce right off it.

dossier.summary: A tadpole that has just grown legs and can't use them yet. Poliwag's skin is thin, damp and so transparent that its coiled insides show through as the swirl on its belly, clearer after it has eaten; yet the skin is so flexible that sharp fangs bounce off it. It lives in water and swims rather than walks. In Ilex Forest it is caught only by fishing, and it lives in Blackthorn City's water too. The direction of the belly spiral is said to differ from region to region.
diet: It eats, and its belly swirl looks clearer afterwards.
behavior: It prefers swimming to standing or walking, and is more adept at it.
social: Poliwag gather from far and wide when they hear Politoed's echoing cry, and Politoed's cries make them obey: the line's adult leads groups of young.
defense: Its skin, though thin, is so flexible that even sharp fangs bounce off it.
habitat: Water: because it is inept at walking on its new legs, it always swims around in water.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by a Water-type move.

about: The swirl on its belly subtly undulates. Staring at it may gradually cause drowsiness.
senses: The skin on most of its body is moist. However, the skin on its belly spiral feels smooth.

about: This strong and skilled swimmer is even capable of crossing the Pacific Ocean just by kicking.
moves: It can use its well-developed arms and legs to run on the surface of the water for a split second.

dossier.summary: Alakazam is a humanoid Psychic Pokémon whose brain never stops growing: its brain cells multiply until it dies, it forgets nothing, and its head becomes too heavy for its neck, so it holds it up by psychokinesis. Its muscles are very weak, it moves its body with psychic power, and it would rather not fight hand to hand. It is the end of a line that begins with Abra, which sleeps 18 hours a day and teleports away from danger even in its sleep. Alakazam only forms when a Kadabra is traded between people, so no Gen I–IV game has a wild one.
diet: A brain that never stops growing must be expensive to run, so its energy needs are probably high; how it meets them is unrecorded.
senses: Closing both its eyes heightens all its other senses, letting it use its abilities to their extremes.
behavior: It calculates many things in order to gain the edge in every battle.
defense: It avoids physical fighting and defeats foes with extrasensory power.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: urban.

abilities: Boosts Attack if there is a status problem.

about: Always brimming with power, it passes time by lifting boulders. Doing so makes it even stronger.
moves: Machop exercises by hefting around a Graveler as if it were a barbell. There are some Machop that travel the world in a quest to master all kinds of martial arts.

abilities: Boosts Attack if there is a status problem.
Ensures both Pokémon’s and foe’s attacks land.

about: It always goes at its full power, but this very tough and durable Pokémon never gets tired.
senses: The muscles covering its body teem with power. Even when still, it exudes an amazing sense of strength.
moves: It happily carries heavy cargo to toughen up. It willingly does hard work for people.

abilities: Boosts Attack if there is a status problem.
Ensures both Pokémon’s and foe’s attacks land.

about: It quickly swings its four arms to rock its opponents with ceaseless punches and chops from all angles.
moves: Machamp has the power to hurl anything aside. However, trying to do any work requiring care and dexterity causes its arms to get tangled. This Pokémon tends to leap into action before it thinks.
defense: It is impossible to defend against punches and chops doled out by its four arms. Its fighting spirit flares up when it faces a tough opponent.

dossier.summary: Machamp is a four-armed, 130 kg mountain fighter: its arms react faster than it can think and can throw a thousand punches in two seconds, and once it pins a foe's limbs the fight is all but over. It is strong enough to hurl almost anything aside, yet hopeless at careful work with its fingers, which tangle when it tries. The line lives for training: Machop lifts boulders and even Graveler as weights in the mountains, and Machoke, which wears a belt to hold its power in check, willingly does heavy work for people. Machamp forms only when a Machoke is traded, so it is never wild in Gen I–IV.
diet: An animal that is almost all muscle and trains all day must eat a great deal; what it eats is not recorded.
behavior: It tends to leap into action before it thinks.
social: 'Some Machop travel the world' to master martial arts, which reads as dispersal by young animals away from where they were raised.
defense: Its punches and chops from four arms are impossible to defend against.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for the whole line: mountain. Machop lives in the mountains away from humans and trains by lifting rocks there.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: Even though its body is extremely skinny, it is blindingly fast when catching its prey.
eats: Even though its body is extremely skinny, it is blindingly fast when catching its prey.

dossier.summary: A thin, flexible, carnivorous plant that traps and eats bugs: it ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them, blindingly fast when catching prey, and flings a vine at anything it notices moving. It soaks up water through its root feet planted deep in the ground, but can't escape while rooted; instead its thin body bends and sways to avoid any attack, and it spits a corrosive fluid that melts even iron. It prefers hot, humid places. Its bud looks like a human face, which is why it is rumoured to be a legendary mandrake. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 31, 32 and 44 in Johto and Routes 24, 25, 5 and 6 in Kanto.
diet: A carnivorous Pokémon that traps and eats bugs: it ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them.
behavior: If it notices anything that moves, it immediately flings its vine at the object.
social: Nothing is said about Bellsprout living together. Its final form is said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles (71.1).
defense: Its thin and flexible body lets it bend and sway to avoid any attack, however strong.
habitat: Hot and humid places; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: Even though it is filled with acid, it does not melt because it also oozes a protective fluid.
eats: If its prey is bigger than its mouth, it slices up the victim with sharp leaves, then eats every morsel.

dossier.summary: The middle stage of Bellsprout's line: a plant-like flycatcher filled with acid, which does not melt because it also oozes a protective fluid. When hungry it swallows anything that moves and melts it inside; it captures unwary prey by dousing them with toxic powder, and slices up prey too big for its mouth with its razor-sharp leaves, then eats every morsel. At night it hooks its rear onto a tree branch and sleeps there; if it moves in its sleep, it may wake up on the ground. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 44 below Blackthorn and on Kanto's Routes 24 and 25.
diet: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves; its hapless prey is melted inside by strong acids.
senses: It swallows anything that moves: it senses movement, as its young form notices anything that moves (69.5).
behavior: At night it hooks onto a tree branch with its rear and goes to sleep; if it moves around in its sleep, it may wake up to find itself on the ground.
social: Nothing is said about Weepinbell living together. Its final form is said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles (71.1).
defense: It spits Poison Powder to immobilize the enemy and then finishes it with a spray of acid; it spits a fluid that dissolves everything.
habitat: Among trees, where it sleeps hooked to a branch; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: ACID that has dissolved many prey becomes sweeter, making it even more effective at attracting prey.
eats: ACID that has dissolved many prey becomes sweeter, making it even more effective at attracting prey.
senses: It pools in its mouth a fluid with a honeylike scent, which is really an acid that dissolves anything.

Inflicts damage on foes using any draining move.

about: When the tide goes out, dehydrated Tentacool remains can be found washed up on the shore.
senses: It drifts aimlessly in waves. Very difficult to see in water, it may not be noticed until it stings.
moves: As it floats along on the waves, it uses its toxic feelers to stab anything it touches.
defense: It drifts in sea currents. Countless fishermen are hurt by its poison stingers.

dossier.summary: A drifting jellyfish of shallow seas, its body almost entirely water. Tentacool floats along on the waves and currents, very hard to see, and stabs anything it touches with its toxic feelers; anglers and fishermen who hook one by accident are often stung. Out of the sea it dries up like parchment, and when the tide goes out its shriveled remains wash up on the shore. Its crystal-clear eyes shoot beams of light, made, in one entry, by refracting sunlight through the water in its body. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the commonest thing on the surface of the sea in both regions, from New Bark Town and the Whirl Islands to Pallet Town and the seas around Cinnabar.
diet: The machine reading files it as living on sunlight, from 72.7; but that entry turns sunlight into beam energy, not food.
senses: Supersonic (Lv 5) and Screech (Lv 36) are sound moves: the line uses sound, as Tentacruel's orbs do before an ultrasonic blast (73.6).
behavior: It drifts aimlessly in the waves and floats along with the sea currents.
social: Nothing is said about whether Tentacool drift alone or together. The surf tables make them by far the commonest animal on the water, so they meet constantly.
defense: Its toxic feelers stab anything they touch; anglers who hook one are punished by its stinging acid, and countless fishermen are hurt by its stingers.
habitat: Shallow seas, drifting in the waves and sea currents; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Prevents its stats from being lowered.
Inflicts damage on foes using any draining move.

about: Its 80 tentacles absorb water and stretch almost endlessly to constrict its prey and enemies.
eats: Its 80 tentacles absorb water and stretch almost endlessly to constrict its prey and enemies.
defense: With 80 tentacles for ensnaring victims, it prevents escape until the prey is weakened by poison.

dossier.summary: The adult of Tentacool: a jellyfish with 80 tentacles that it keeps short and extends on hunts, stretching them almost endlessly as they absorb water to make a poisonous net that entangles prey and is difficult to escape. It can catch up to 80 prey at once, and weakens them with a harsh toxin. It lives among complex rock formations on the ocean floor. Two large red orbs on its head glow when it is excited or agitated, flash stridently to alert others to danger, and glow before it lashes the area with an ultrasonic blast that raises rough waves. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it shares Tentacool's shores in both regions, rarer and deeper, on the surf and the super rod.
diet: A hunter: on hunts its tentacles are extended to ensnare and immobilize prey, then weaken it with poison.
behavior: It keeps its tentacles short and extends them on hunts.
social: It alerts others to danger by stridently flashing the red orbs on its head.
defense: In battle it extends all 80 tentacles to entrap its opponent inside an encircling poisonous net that is difficult to escape.
habitat: It lives in complex rock formations on the ocean floor; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

It is protected against 1-hit KO attacks.

about: Most people may not notice, but a closer look should reveal that there are many Geodude around.
eats: When Geodude sleeps deeply, it buries itself halfway into the ground. It will not awaken even if hikers step on it unwittingly. In the morning, this Pokémon rolls downhill in search of food.
moves: It uses its arms to steadily climb steep mountain paths. It swings its fists around if angered.

dossier.summary: A rock with arms. Geodude lives on mountain trails and in caves, looks so much like a boulder that hikers step on it, and swings its fists at them when they do. It hauls itself up steep paths with its arms, sleeps half-buried in the ground, and in the morning rolls downhill to look for food; its next stage, Graveler, is said to eat rock, preferring rock covered in moss. On Route 45 and at the Blackthorn end of Dark Cave it is one of the most frequent encounters, and one entry says there are many more around than people notice.
diet: In the morning it rolls downhill in search of food.
senses: It keeps an eye on climbers from where it lies half buried, so it watches its surroundings; nothing more is said about its senses.
behavior: When it sleeps deeply it buries itself halfway into the ground, and does not wake even if hikers step on it.
social: Proud of their sturdy bodies, they bash against each other in contests to prove whose is harder.
defense: It looks just like a rock at rest and is said to be impossible to tell from one; people mistake it for a boulder.
habitat: Found in fields and mountains, and commonly near mountain trails.

abilities: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.

about: With a free and uncaring nature, it doesn't mind if pieces break off while it rolls down mountains.
eats: It tumbles down slopes, heedless of any body parts chipping off. It eats a ton of rocks daily.
moves: Rocks are Graveler’s favorite food. This Pokémon will climb a mountain from the base to the summit, crunchingly feasting on rocks all the while. Upon reaching the peak, it rolls back down to the bottom.

dossier.summary: The heavy, rolling middle stage of the Geodude line, and the only animal in the highlands community whose diet is plainly stated as rock. Graveler eats a ton of rock a day and prefers rock covered in moss; it climbs a mountain eating as it goes, then rolls back down, flattening whatever is in its way. It makes its home in rows of horizontal holes it gouges in sheer cliffs. On Route 45 it has the highest encounter rate of any Pokémon in both HeartGold and SoulSilver.
diet: It grows by feeding on rocks, its favourite food, and eats its way through a ton of rock a day.
senses: It pays no attention to objects in its path; nothing is said about how it perceives.
behavior: A slow walker, it rolls to move.
defense: Sturdy and Rock Head; Defense Curl, Self-Destruct (Lv 18) and Explosion (Lv 38).
habitat: Mountains: trails, steep slopes and the paths it rolls down.

abilities: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.

about: It is a weak runner immediately after birth. It gradually becomes faster by chasing after its parents.
senses: Its hind legs, which have hooves that are harder than diamond, kick back at any presence it senses behind it.
moves: Its legs grow strong while it chases after its parent. It runs in fields and mountains all day.

moves: Just loves to run. If it sees some thing faster than itself, it will give chase at top speed.

about: It lazes vacantly near water. If something bites its tail, it won't even notice for a whole day.
eats: It catches prey by dipping its tail in water at the side of a river. But it often forgets what it is doing and spends entire days just loafing at water’s edge.
senses: Although slow, it is skilled at fishing with its tail. It does not feel pain if its tail is bitten.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from becoming confused.

about: If the tail-biting Shellder is thrown off in a harsh battle, it reverts to being an ordinary Slowpoke.
eats: Its tail has a Shellder firmly attached with a bite. As a result, the tail can’t be used for fishing anymore. This forces it to reluctantly swim and catch prey.
senses: Naturally dull to begin with, it lost its ability to feel pain due to Shellder's seeping poison.
moves: Its tail has a Shellder firmly attached with a bite. As a result, the tail can’t be used for fishing anymore. This forces it to reluctantly swim and catch prey.
defense: Naturally dull to begin with, it lost its ability to feel pain due to Shellder's seeping poison.

dossier.summary: A Slowpoke with a Shellder clamped on its tail, and the Pokédex's clearest case of two species making one animal. A Slowpoke went hunting in the sea, a Shellder bit its tail, and it became Slowbro. The Shellder won't let go because of the tasty flavour oozing from the tail, and is said to feed on Slowbro's leftover scraps; its seeping poison has left Slowbro unable to feel pain. With the tail no longer usable for fishing, Slowbro has to swim and catch its prey instead. If the Shellder is thrown off, it becomes an ordinary Slowpoke again. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Slowpoke Well and the Seafoam Islands.
diet: With the Shellder on its tail, the tail can't be used for fishing any more, so Slowbro grudgingly swims and catches prey instead.
senses: It can't feel pain, because of the Shellder's poison.
behavior: It lives lazily and is naturally dull, usually dim-witted, but it seems to become inspired when the Shellder on its tail bites down.
social: Its one partnership is with the Shellder on its tail.
defense: It lost its ability to feel pain because of Shellder's seeping poison.
habitat: It lives lazily by the sea; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.

abilities: It is protected against 1-hit KO attacks.

about: It is attracted by electromagnetic waves. It may approach trainers if they are using their POKéGEAR.
eats: The units at its sides generate electromagnetic waves that keep it airborne. It feeds on electricity.
moves: Magnemite floats in the air by emitting electromagnetic waves from the units at its sides. These waves block gravity. This Pokémon becomes incapable of flight if its internal electrical supply is depleted.

abilities: It is protected against 1-hit KO attacks.

moves: If it eats the plant stalk it carries as emergency rations, it runs off in search of a new stalk.

moves: It lives on a grassy plain where it can see a long way. If it sees an enemy, it runs away at 60 mph.

about: It collects data and plans three times as wisely, but it may think too much and fall into a state of immobility.
eats: If one of the heads gets to eat, the others will be satisfied, too, and they will stop squabbling.
senses: An enemy that takes its eyes off any of the three heads--even for a second--will get pecked severely.
moves: When Doduo evolves into this odd breed, one of its heads splits into two. It runs at nearly 40 mph.

Heals status problems if it is raining.

about: Although it can't walk well on land, it is a graceful swimmer. It especially loves being in frigid seas.
eats: Seel hunt for prey in frigid, ice-covered seas. When it needs to breathe, it punches a hole through the ice with the sharply protruding section of its head.
moves: In daytime, it is often found asleep on the seabed in shallow waters. Its nostrils close while it swims.
defense: The protruding horn on its head is very hard. It is used for bashing through thick icebergs.

dossier.summary: A white-and-blue sea lion of frigid, ice-covered seas. Seel loves the cold, relishing water around -10 °C and staying active at -40 °F, and wears light blue fur and a thick, tough hide against it. It hunts prey under sheets of ice and, when it needs to breathe, punches a hole through the ice with the hard, sharply protruding horn on its head. Clumsy on land, it is a graceful swimmer; by day it is often found asleep on the seabed in shallow water, nostrils closed. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is the commonest animal of the Seafoam Islands, and lives in the Whirl Islands and off Route 47 too.
diet: It hunts for prey in the frigid sea underneath sheets of ice.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Finding prey under ice, and the way back to its breathing hole, implies good underwater senses.
behavior: In the daytime it is often found asleep on the seabed in shallow waters.
defense: Nothing in its entries describes defence; a thick hide and the cold it can bear are its protection.
habitat: Frigid, iceberg-filled seas; it lives on icebergs. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Ups resistance to Fire-​ and Ice-type moves.
Heals status problems if it is raining.

about: Its streamlined body has little drag in water. The colder the temperature, the friskier it gets.
eats: It sleeps under shallow ocean waters during the day, then looks for food at night when it's cold.
senses: It loves to snooze on bitterly cold ice. The sight of this Pokémon sleeping on a glacier was mistakenly thought to be a mermaid by a mariner long ago.
moves: It stores thermal energy in the body. It swims at a steady eight knots even in intensely cold waters.

dossier.summary: The pure white adult of Seel, a streamlined swimmer of frigid seas with ice floes. Dewgong stores thermal energy in its body and swims a steady eight knots even in intensely cold water; the colder it gets, the friskier and more active it becomes. It sleeps under shallow water by day and looks for food at night when it is cold, loves to snooze on bitterly cold ice, and its white coat hides it from predators in snow. A mariner long ago mistook one asleep on a glacier for a mermaid. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Seafoam Islands.
diet: It looks for food at night, when it's cold.
behavior: It sleeps under shallow ocean waters during the day, then looks for food at night when it's cold.
defense: In snow, its pure white coat obscures it from predators.
habitat: Frigid seas with ice floes; it snoozes on bitterly cold ice and on glaciers. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.
