Protects the Pokémon from item theft.

about: As it moves, it loses bits of its body from which new Grimer emerge. This worsens the stench around it.
eats: Born from polluted sludge in the sea, Grimer’s favorite food is anything filthy. They feed on wastewater pumped out from factories.

abilities: The stench helps keep wild Pokémon away.
Protects the Pokémon from item theft.

about: They love to gather in smelly areas where sludge accumulates, making the stench around them worse.
eats: This Pokémon’s favorite food is anything that is repugnantly filthy. In dirty towns where people think nothing of throwing away litter on the streets, Muk are certain to gather.
senses: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration, it lost its sense of smell.
defense: Its body is made of a powerful poison. Touching it accidentally will cause a fever that requires bed rest.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.
Increases the frequency of multi-strike moves.

about: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.
moves: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.
defense: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.

dossier.summary: A small bivalve in a two-piece shell harder than diamond, tender inside, with a large tongue it always keeps hanging out. Shellder swims backward, surprisingly fast, by opening and closing its shell; at night it burrows a hole in the seafloor sand with its broad tongue and sleeps in it, shell shut and tongue out. Sand caught in its shell becomes beautiful pearls. It is the Shellder that bites a Slowpoke's tail or head that makes Slowbro and Slowking, and that Shellder is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps and on the tasty flavour oozing from its tail. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods along both regions' coasts, beside Chinchou.
diet: The Shellder latched onto a Slowpoke's tail is said to feed on the host's leftover scraps, and won't let go because of the tasty flavour that oozes out of the tail (Slowbro's entries).
behavior: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell, and is surprisingly fast.
social: Its one recorded partnership is with Slowpoke: it bites a Slowpoke's tail and holds on, making Slowbro; on a Slowpoke's head, Slowking.
defense: Its hard shell can withstand any attack; it is vulnerable only when the shell is open and the tender body exposed.
habitat: The sea floor, where it burrows in the sand at night; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.
Increases the frequency of multi-strike moves.

about: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.
moves: It swims in the sea by swallowing water, then jetting it out toward the rear. The Cloyster shoots spikes from its shell using the same system.
defense: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

about: With its gas-like body, it can sneak into any place it desires. However, it can be blown away by wind.
eats: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.
defense: Born from gases, anyone would faint if engulfed by its gaseous body, which contains poison.

dossier.summary: A body that is 95% gas, poisonous, almost invisible and almost weightless (1.3 m across but only 0.1 kg). Gastly can sneak into any place it likes, and it overpowers animals of any size by enveloping them: they faint, suffocate or are slowly poisoned through the skin, and one entry says it can topple an Indian elephant in two seconds. Its weakness is wind, which blows its body away, so groups cluster under the eaves of houses for shelter. It is the first stage of SoulSilver's Gengar. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it haunts Sprout Tower and Bell Tower, at night only.
diet: It envelops its prey in its gas, which suffocates it or slowly weakens it by poisoning it through the skin.
behavior: With its gas-like body it can sneak into any place it desires.
social: Groups of Gastly cluster under the eaves of houses to escape the wind.
defense: Its poison gas is its defence as well as its weapon: it defeats even the largest foes by enveloping them.
habitat: It is said to appear in decrepit, deserted buildings; groups cluster under the eaves of houses. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

about: In total darkness, where nothing is visible, Haunter lurks, silently stalking its next victim.
eats: It licks with its gaseous tongue to steal the victim’s life force. It lurks in darkness for prey.

dossier.summary: The middle stage of the Gengar line, and the most plainly predatory: Haunter lurks in total darkness, silently stalking its next victim, and steals life force by licking with a tongue made of gas. A victim it licks or touches starts shaking and can't stop, until death in the older entries. It slips through walls and lurks inside them to watch, and if one beckons you while floating in the dark, the entries say never to go. It still weighs only 0.1 kg. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 8, at night, one encounter in three.
diet: It licks with its gaseous tongue to steal the victim's life force; it will try to lick a person and steal their life away.
senses: It stalks in total darkness, where nothing is visible, so it finds its victims by something other than sight; what is not said.
behavior: In total darkness Haunter lurks, silently stalking its next victim.
social: Nothing is said about groups; every entry describes a lone stalker.
habitat: Darkness: total darkness where nothing is visible, and the inside of walls. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

about: It steals heat from its surroundings. If you feel a sudden chill, it is certain that a Gengar appeared.
eats: To steal the life of its target, it slips into the prey's shadow and silently waits for an opportunity.
senses: It steals heat from its surroundings. If you feel a sudden chill, it is certain that a Gengar appeared.
moves: The leer that floats in darkness belongs to a Gengar delighting in casting curses on people.

dossier.summary: A night-active shadow-dweller that feeds, by every account, on the warmth and life of other creatures. Gengar slips into its target's shadow and waits, absorbing heat until the victim shivers; a sudden chill is the classic sign that one is near. It also plays: on full-moon nights it mimics people's shadows and laughs at their fright, or runs past them under a streetlight pretending to be their shadow. Its line begins as Gastly, a body that is 95% gas, poisonous to breathe, and so light that strong wind blows it apart; in Johto they shelter in the old towers of Violet and Ecruteak and come out only at night.
diet: It takes heat: Gengar steals warmth from its surroundings and absorbs the heat of people whose shadows it hides in, leaving them shaking with cold.
senses: It operates where nothing is visible: Haunter stalks in total darkness, and Gengar ambushes from shadow, so it does not seem to rely on light.
behavior: Night-active: it hides in shadows at night, and the full moon brings out its shadow mimicry.
social: Gastly gather in groups under the eaves of houses to shelter from wind.
defense: Concealment is its first defence: it hides in shadows, and Haunter lurks inside walls to watch its foes.
habitat: Shadows and darkness, often in human places: the shadowy corners of rooms, people's own shadows, streets lit by streetlights. Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.
It is protected against 1-hit KO attacks.

about: It twists and squirms through the ground. The thunderous roar of its tunneling echoes a long way.
eats: It squirms through the ground using its long and rugged body. It always eats while burrowing.
moves: As it digs through the ground, it absorbs many hard objects. This is what makes its body so solid.

dossier.summary: A rock snake nearly nine metres long that bores through the ground at 50 mph, always eating as it burrows: it feeds on large boulders and absorbs the hard objects it digs through, which is what makes its body so solid. As it grows, the stone parts of its body harden like black diamond, and with age it becomes rounder and smoother. A magnet in its brain acts as a compass so it never loses direction underground. Its tunnelling roars and shakes the ground, and the tunnels it leaves become homes for Diglett. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Union Cave, on Route 47 and Mt. Silver in Johto, and in Rock Tunnel and Victory Road in Kanto.
diet: It always eats while burrowing, searching for food as it bores through the ground, and feeds on large boulders.
senses: A magnetic sense of direction, from the magnet in its brain.
behavior: It rapidly bores through the ground at 50 mph by squirming and twisting its massive body.
defense: Its size and its solid, diamond-hard body.
habitat: It usually lives underground; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from falling asleep.
Determines what moves the foe has.

about: If you think that you had a good dream, but you can't remember it, a Drowzee has probably eaten it.
eats: It remembers every dream it eats. It rarely eats the dreams of adults because children's are much tastier.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from falling asleep.
Determines what moves the foe has.

about: When it is very hungry, it puts humans it meets to sleep, then it feasts on their dreams.
eats: The arcing movement and glitter of the pendulum in a Hypno’s hand lull the foe into deep hypnosis. While searching for prey, it polishes the pendulum.
senses: When it locks eyes with an enemy, it will use a mix of PSI moves such as HypnoSIS and CONFUSION.
moves: It carries a pendulum-like device. There once was an incident in which it took away a child it hypnotized.

abilities: Prevents the Attack stat from being lowered.
The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.

about: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.
eats: If it is unable to find food, it will absorb nutrients by swallowing a mouthful of sand.
senses: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.

dossier.summary: A small red beach crab that lives in holes dug in the sand. Krabby's pincers are weapons and also its balance when it walks sideways; they break off easily but grow back fast, though one that has lost a pincer somehow can't walk sideways any more. When danger comes it cloaks itself in bubbles to look bigger. On sandy shores with little food Krabby squabble over territory, and one that can't find food will swallow a mouthful of sand for its nutrients. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished all along Johto's coast and Kanto's Sea Route 19, and lives in the Seafoam Islands.
diet: If it can't find food, it absorbs nutrients by swallowing a mouthful of sand.
senses: It senses danger approaching; how is not described.
social: On sandy shores with little food, Krabby can be seen squabbling with each other over territory.
defense: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.
habitat: Sandy beaches near the sea, in burrows dug into the sand. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.

abilities: Prevents the Attack stat from being lowered.
The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.

about: It can hardly lift its massive, overgrown pincer. The pincer's size makes it difficult to aim properly.

dossier.summary: The adult of Krabby, a crab with one claw grown massively, as hard as steel and said to have 10,000 horsepower of crushing force. The claw is too heavy for its own good: Kingler can hardly lift it, finds it hard to aim, staggers if it raises it too fast, tires quickly, and outside battle the claw just gets in the way. It waves the claw in the air to communicate with others. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished along Johto's coasts and in Kanto it is the commonest Rock Smash find on Sea Route 19; it lives in the Seafoam Islands too.
diet: A claw that crushes with great force would crack shellfish and hard prey, but no entry says it does.
behavior: If it lifts the pincers too fast, it loses its balance and staggers; because the claw is so heavy, it quickly tires.
social: It waves its huge claw in the air to communicate with others.
defense: The claw is its weapon: very powerful in battle.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge; its young live in burrows on sandy beaches (98.6).

abilities: Gives full immunity to all sound-based moves.
Contact with the Pokémon may cause paralysis.

about: It rolls to move. If the ground is uneven, a sudden jolt from hitting a bump can cause it to explode.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all sound-based moves.
Contact with the Pokémon may cause paralysis.

about: It is dangerous. If it has too much electricity and has nothing to do, it amuses itself by exploding.
eats: They appear in great numbers at electric power plants. Because they feed on electricity, they cause massive and chaotic blackouts in nearby cities.
senses: Electrode eats electricity in the atmosphere. On days when lightning strikes, you can see this Pokémon exploding all over the place from eating too much electricity.

dossier.summary: A red-and-white ball that eats electricity and explodes. Electrode stores an overflowing amount of electric energy under very high pressure, and even a small shock sets it off; with too much charge and nothing to do it amuses itself by exploding. It eats electricity from the atmosphere, so on days of lightning they explode all over the place from eating too much, and they gather in great numbers at power plants to feed on fresh electricity, causing blackouts in nearby cities. Bloated with charge, it drifts on the wind. It is feared as 'The Bomb Ball'. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Cerulean Cave, one encounter in twenty.
diet: Electrode eats electricity in the atmosphere.
senses: It is attracted to electricity, so it senses where electricity is.
behavior: If it has too much electricity and nothing to do, it amuses itself by exploding.
social: They congregate in great numbers at power plants: a feeding aggregation, not described as a social group.
defense: It is dangerous: it explodes. Self-Destruct (Lv 29) and Explosion (Lv 51) are the explosions in game form; Static paralyses what touches it.
habitat: Power plants, where they gather to feed; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is urban.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: Their shells are very durable. Even if they crack, they can survive without spilling their contents.
defense: The shell is very durable. Even if it cracks, it can survive without spilling the contents.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.

about: Its three heads think independently. However, they are friendly and never appear to squabble.

abilities: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.
The Pokémon draws in all Electric-type moves.

about: If it is sad or lonely, the skull it wears shakes, and emits a plaintive and mournful sound.
senses: It pines for the mother it will never see again. Seeing a likeness of its mother in the full moon, it cries. The stains on the skull it wears are from its tears.

dossier.summary: A small, lonely Pokémon that lost its mother after its birth and always wears her skull, so no one has ever seen its real face. Cubone pines for the mother it will never see again: when it thinks of her it cries, its cries echo inside the skull as a sad melody, and seeing her likeness in the full moon it weeps; the stains on the skull are its tears. When it is lonesome it is said to cry loudly. Marowak is the Cubone that has overcome that grief and grown tough. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Kanto's Rock Tunnel, with Marowak, Onix, Geodude and Machop.
diet: The machine reading's rock-eater comes from its Ground type alone; nothing supports it.
senses: It sees a likeness of its mother in the full moon: it sees well enough at night to see the moon's face.
behavior: When it thinks of its dead mother, it cries, and its crying makes the skull rattle hollowly; its cries echo inside the skull and come out as a sad melody.
social: Lonely by name and by its entries: it lost its mother after its birth and pines for her.
defense: The skull helmet covers its head and face.
habitat: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.

abilities: Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.
The Pokémon draws in all Electric-type moves.

about: It has been seen pounding boulders with the bone it carries in order to tap out messages to others.
moves: It has been seen pounding boulders with the bone it carries in order to tap out messages to others.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from paralysis.
Powers up moves that have recoil damage.

about: This amazing POKé MON has an awesome sense of balance. It can kick in succession from any position.
senses: This amazing POKé MON has an awesome sense of balance. It can kick in succession from any position.
moves: When in a hurry, its legs lengthen progressively. It runs smoothly with extra long, loping strides.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from losing accuracy.
Boosts the power of punching moves.

about: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.
eats: Its punches slice the air. They are launched at such high speed, even a slight graze could cause a burn.
senses: While apparently doing nothing, it fires punches in lightning fast volleys that are impossible to see.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from becoming confused.

about: Its tongue has well-developed nerves that run to the very tip, so it can be deftly manipulated.
eats: Its tongue is twice the length of its body. It can be moved like an arm for grabbing food and attacking.
senses: Whenever it sees something unfamiliar, it always licks the object because it memorizes things by texture and taste. It is somewhat put off by sour things.
moves: Its tongue has well-developed nerves that run to the very tip, so it can be deftly manipulated.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

about: Its thin, filmy body is filled with gases that cause constant sniffles, coughs and teary eyes.
senses: Its thin, filmy body is filled with gases that cause constant sniffles, coughs and teary eyes.
defense: Koffing embodies toxic substances. It mixes the toxins with raw garbage to set off a chemical reaction that results in a terribly powerful poison gas. The higher the temperature, the more gas is concocted by this Pokémon.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all Ground-type moves.

about: If one of the twin Koffing inflates, the other one deflates. It constantly mixes its poisonous gases.
senses: When it inhales poisonous gases from garbage, its body expands, and its insides smell much worse.
defense: Top-grade perfume is made using its internal poison gases by diluting them to the highest level.

abilities: The Pokémon draws in all Electric-type moves.
Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.

about: It is inept at turning because of its four short legs. It can only charge and run in one direction.
senses: Rhyhorn runs in a straight line, smashing everything in its path. It is not bothered even if it rushes headlong into a block of steel. This Pokémon may feel some pain from the collision the next day, however.
moves: It is inept at turning because of its four short legs. It can only charge and run in one direction.

abilities: The Pokémon draws in all Electric-type moves.
Protects the Pokémon from recoil damage.

about: Its rugged hide protects it from even the heat of lava. However, the hide also makes it insensitive.
defense: Its brain developed after it stood up on its hind legs. Its drill horn bores tunnels through solid rock.

abilities: All status problems heal when it switches out.
Boosts the likelihood of added effects appearing.

about: It walks carefully to prevent its egg from breaking. However, it is extremely fast at running away.
senses: A gentle and kindhearted Pokémon that shares its nutritious eggs if it sees an injured Pokémon.

dossier.summary: A rare, gentle, all-female Pokémon that lays nutritious eggs every day, several a day, and gives them away: it shares them with injured Pokémon and people, and won't share them with those who have evil in their hearts. The eggs are so delicious that even people who have lost their appetite eat them eagerly, which is why people try to catch it. It walks carefully so as not to break its egg, but runs away extremely fast. It is said to bring happiness to whoever catches one. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Kanto's Routes 13, 14 and 15, one encounter in a hundred, and comes to Route 13 in swarms.
diet: Laying several nutritious eggs a day needs a great deal of food; what it eats to do so is a gap.
senses: It sees an injured Pokémon and shares its eggs, and it tells those with evil in their hearts, by the entries; how is not said.
behavior: It is extremely fast at running away.
social: It shares its nutritious eggs with injured Pokémon and people.
defense: It runs: carefully walking with its egg, it is extremely fast at running away.
habitat: It is rare and rarely found; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is urban.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in sunshine.
Prevents problems with status in sunny weather.

about: The vines that cloak its entire body are always jiggling. They effectively unnerve its foes.

dossier.summary: A walking mass of thick blue vines, wide like seaweed and covered in fine hair, that hides whatever is inside: no one has seen the face behind them. The vines are always jiggling and swaying; they unnerve foes, tangle any moving thing that gets close, and tickle whoever is caught. Grabbed, they snap off painlessly so it can get away, and grow back the very next day; they are said never to stop growing. Its adult, Tangrowth, stands still like a shrub and ensnares prey that wanders near. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Route 44 below Blackthorn, on Route 28 and Mt. Silver, in the grass of Sea Route 21, and in the trees of the routes around Fuchsia.
diet: Grass-typed with Chlorophyll and Leaf Guard, and Absorb (Lv 8), Mega Drain (Lv 26) and Ingrain in its list: in game terms a sun-fed plant that can root and drain.
senses: It tangles any moving thing: it senses movement, in some way.
behavior: Its vines are always jiggling and shake or sway as it walks.
defense: Its jiggling vines effectively unnerve its foes; in battle it moves them constantly to annoy its opponent.
habitat: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.

abilities: The Pokémon awakens quickly from sleep.
Enables moves to hit Ghost-type foes.

about: If it is safe, the young gets out of the belly pouch to play. The adult keeps a close eye on the youngster.
senses: It raises its offspring in its belly pouch. It lets the baby out to play only when it feels safe.
moves: To avoid crushing the baby it carries in its pouch, it always sleeps standing up.
defense: To protect its young, it will never give up during battle, no matter how badly wounded it is.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in rain.
Powers up moves if they become critical hits.

about: If attacked by a larger enemy, it quickly swims to safety by adeptly controlling its well-developed dorsal fin.
eats: Horsea eats small insects and moss off of rocks. If the ocean current turns fast, this Pokémon anchors itself by wrapping its tail around rocks or coral to prevent being washed away.
senses: It makes its nest in the shade of corals. If it senses danger, it spits murky ink and flees.
moves: If attacked by a larger enemy, it quickly swims to safety by adeptly controlling its well-developed dorsal fin.

dossier.summary: A small sea-horse of coral and rock, the first stage of the rival's Kingdra. Horsea eats small insects and moss off rocks, and is known to shoot down flying bugs with precision blasts of ink from the surface. It swims by flicking the fins on its back, moving in any direction or even backwards while still facing forward, anchors itself with its coiled tail when the current runs fast, and nests in the shade of corals. When danger comes it sprays a dense black ink and flees. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands and the deepest floor of the Seafoam Islands.
diet: Horsea eats small insects and moss off of rocks.
senses: It senses danger quickly enough to ink reflexively, and aims ink precisely at flying bugs from under the surface, so it sees well through water and air.
behavior: If attacked by a larger enemy, it quickly swims to safety by adeptly controlling its dorsal fin.
social: When they're in a safe location, they can be seen playfully tangling their tails together.
defense: If it senses danger, it reflexively sprays a dense black ink, or murky ink, and tries to escape.
habitat: The sea, among coral and rock: it nests in the shade of corals and anchors to rocks; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may poison the foe.
Powers up moves if they become critical hits.

about: An examination of its cells revealed the presence of a gene not found in Horsea. It became a hot topic.
eats: Seadra generates whirlpools by spinning its body. The whirlpools are strong enough to swallow even fishing boats. This Pokémon weakens prey with these currents, then swallows it whole.
moves: Capable of swim ming backwards by rapidly flapping its wing-like pectoral fins and stout tail.
defense: Its fin-tips leak poison. Its fins and bones are highly valued as ingredients in herbal medicine.

dossier.summary: The spiny, poisonous middle stage of the Kingdra line. Seadra's body bristles with poison barbs and spikes that can make a careless person faint; it sleeps wedged between coral branches with its tail hooked on, and it spins its body to make whirlpools strong enough to swallow fishing boats, weakening prey in the current and then swallowing it whole. The male raises the young and shows no mercy to anything approaching the nest. Its fins and bones are prized in traditional medicine. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the Whirl Islands and on the Seafoam Islands' deepest floor.
diet: It generates whirlpools by spinning its body, weakens prey with the currents, then swallows it whole.
behavior: It sleeps after wriggling itself between the branches of coral, hooking its tail to coral to stay in place.
social: The male raises the young; if approached, it fends off the intruder with its toxic spikes.
defense: Its spines provide protection; carelessly touching it can cause fainting from the spikes.
habitat: Coral reefs: it sleeps between coral branches, and coral harvesters get stung when they fail to notice it. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in rain.
Prevents the Pokémon from getting a burn.

about: Its dorsal, pectoral and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the water dancer.
senses: It swims at a steady 5 knots. If it senses danger, it will strike back with its sharp horn.
moves: It swims elegantly by flittering its tail fin as if it were a dress. It has the look of a queen.
defense: Though it appears very elegant when swimming with fins unfurled, it can jab powerfully with its horn.

dossier.summary: A river fish with a single sharp horn, admired for fins that billow like a ballgown. Goldeen are strong swimmers that hold a steady five knots up fast streams, and at spawning time they swim up rivers and waterfalls in schools. The elegance is deceptive: it rams hard enough with its horn to shatter aquarium glass. In the highlands it is the common fish of Dark Cave's water, caught there with every rod, and nothing records what it eats.
diet: Its first level-up move is Peck (Lv 1), and later Fury Attack (Lv 31): pecking strikes that might double as the way it picks at food, though nothing says so.
behavior: A strong swimmer that holds a steady five knots (about 9 km/h), even up fast streams.
social: It schools: in spring, schools of Goldeen swim up falls and rivers, and at egg-laying time they travel upstream in large groups.
defense: The horn: it rams and jabs when threatened.
habitat: Rivers and ponds, and fast streams it can swim up nonstop.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in rain.
Prevents the Pokémon from getting a burn.

about: During spawning season, Seaking gather from all over, causing rivers to appear a brilliant red.
defense: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

dossier.summary: The adult of the Goldeen line, a horned river fish whose life centres on its nest. In autumn Seaking gather from all over to spawn, turning the rivers red; the male bores a hole in a riverbed boulder with his drill-like horn, and the pair take turns guarding the eggs for over a month. It defends its eggs with its life. In the highlands it is a rare Super Rod catch in Dark Cave's water, where there are no riverbed boulders to nest in.
diet: It fattens before the autumn courtship, so it must feed heavily in the months before spawning.
behavior: In the autumn spawning season they swim powerfully up rivers and creeks.
social: During spawning season Seaking gather from all over, colouring the rivers a brilliant red.
defense: To protect its family it will fight with its drill-sharp horn.
habitat: Rivers, creeks and stream beds; it lives in hollowed rocks in streams.

abilities: Raises the likelihood of meeting wild Pokémon.
All status problems heal when it switches out.

about: At night, the middle of its body slowly flickers with the same rhythm as a human heartbeat.
moves: When the stars twinkle at night, it floats up from the sea floor, and its body's center core flickers.

abilities: Raises the likelihood of meeting wild Pokémon.
All status problems heal when it switches out.

about: The middle section of its body is called the core. It glows in a different color each time it is seen.
moves: Starmie swims through water by spinning its star-shaped body as if it were a propeller on a ship. The core at the center of this Pokémon’s body glows in seven colors.

abilities: Gives full immunity to all sound-based moves.

about: A skilled mime from birth, it gains the ability to create invisible objects as it matures.

abilities: Powers up Bug-type moves in a pinch.
Powers up the Pokémon’s weaker moves.

about: It slashes through grass with its sharp scythes, moving too fast for the human eye to track.
eats: It tears and shreds prey with its wickedly sharp scythes. It very rarely spreads its wings to fly.
moves: It tears and shreds prey with its wickedly sharp scythes. It very rarely spreads its wings to fly.

dossier.summary: A green mantis-like hunter of tall grass. Scyther hides in the grass, where its colours make it invisible, then leaps out and slices prey with twin scythes on its forearms, moving too fast for the eye to follow; its speed adds to the scythes' sharpness, and cutting hard things makes them sharper still. It can cut thick logs in one stroke, and it very rarely spreads its wings to fly. It is the young of SoulSilver's Scizor. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it appears only in the Bug-Catching Contest at the National Park, which stocks it, so Johto has no resident population.
diet: It leaps out of tall grass and slices prey with its scythes; it tears and shreds prey.
behavior: It slashes through grass with its scythes, moving too fast for the human eye to track; when it moves it leaves only a blur.
social: Nothing is said about groups; every entry describes a lone ambusher.
defense: Camouflage in grass, and speed: it hides, and when seen it is a blur.
habitat: Tall grass, which it hides in and leaps out of; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.

abilities: Determines what moves the foe has.

about: It rocks its body rhythmically. It appears to alter the rhythm depending on how it is feeling.

dossier.summary: A humanoid Ice and Psychic Pokémon, every one of them female, that moves as if dancing and appears to use the dance to communicate. Its cries sound like human speech and come in several patterns that seem to carry different meanings, but nobody has worked out what it says. The dancing is contagious: people who watch it find themselves swaying along without meaning to. Nothing in the Pokédex says what it eats or how a species without males reproduces. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is an uncommon find on every floor of the Ice Path, met more often by day.
diet: Its wild moves are close-contact ones: Pound, Lick (Lv 5), Double Slap (Lv 15), Ice Punch (Lv 18), Body Slam (Lv 39), Wring Out (Lv 44), with Lovely Kiss (Lv 8), which puts a target to sleep, and Mean Look (Lv 21), which stops it escaping. If it takes animal food, the kit fits capture at arm's length.
senses: Forewarn reads as a sense: it perceives what an opponent can do before the opponent acts.
behavior: It moves to a rhythm of its own, sashaying as if it were dancing.
social: It seems to use dancing to communicate.
defense: Forewarn lets it determine what moves a foe has: an early warning of what it is facing. It also has Oblivious.
habitat: In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on all four Ice Path floors (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F): 5% at any time plus another 5% by day, Lv 22-23. It is also on Seafoam Islands B4F (12%, Lv 38-40).

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause paralysis.

about: Electricity runs across the surface of its body. In darkness, its entire body glows a whitish-blue.
eats: Half of all blackouts occur when this Pokémon appears at power plants and eats electricity.
moves: Electricity runs across the surface of its body. In darkness, its entire body glows a whitish-blue.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may burn the foe.

about: It dislikes cold places, so it blows scorching flames to make the environment suitable for itself.
senses: When it breathes deeply, heat waves form around its body, making it hard to see clearly.

abilities: Prevents the Attack stat from being lowered.
Moves can be used regardless of abilities.

about: With its pincer horns, it digs burrows to sleep in at night. In the morning, damp soil clings to its body.
eats: It grips prey with its pincers until the prey is torn in half. What it can’t tear, it tosses far.
moves: With its pincer horns, it digs burrows to sleep in at night. In the morning, damp soil clings to its body.

abilities: Raises Attack upon taking a critical hit.

about: They fight each other by locking horns. The herd's protector takes pride in its battle-scarred horns.

abilities: Boosts the Pokémon’s Speed in rain.

about: An underpowered, pathetic Pokémon. It may jump high on rare occasions, but usually not more than seven feet.
senses: Its swimming muscles are weak, so it is easily washed away by currents. In places where water pools, you can see many Magikarp deposited there by the flow.
moves: A Magikarp living for many years can leap a mountain using Splash. The move remains useless, though.

dossier.summary: A fish that does almost nothing but flop and splash, and the Pokédex's favourite example of weakness. Its swimming muscles are weak, so currents push it along and wash it into pools in numbers, and it jumps for no reason, which makes it easy for predators like Pidgeotto to catch. Yet it is hardy enough to survive in any body of water, however polluted, and it lives in seas, lakes, rivers and puddles alike. In Ilex Forest it is the commonest catch on an Old Rod, and it is in Blackthorn City's water too.
diet: A fish that can't swim against even slow currents probably eats whatever it can reach without chasing: drifting food, plants or small animals.
behavior: It flops and splashes about, for no reason anyone can see.
social: Many gather where currents deposit them, but that is passive aggregation, not described social life.
defense: Practically none: it is virtually worthless in both power and speed, and its jumping makes it easy for predators like Pidgeotto to catch mid-jump.
habitat: Seas, lakes, rivers and shallow puddles: any body of water, however polluted.

about: They say that during past strife, Gyarados would appear and leave blazing ruins in its wake.

dossier.summary: The adult of Magikarp, and the Pokédex's great example of transformation: a 6.5 m, 235 kg sea serpent of extreme violence. Every entry is about rage. Once it appears it rampages until it has demolished everything around it, sometimes for a month, burning places down even in a storm; the old entries and legends tie its appearances to human wars and strife. When Magikarp evolves, its brain cells change structure, which is said to explain the violence. No entry says what it eats. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is fished from the Lake of Rage, Mt. Silver, Fuchsia, Cerulean Cave and the Seafoam Islands, and a red one waits at the Lake of Rage. It was in SoulSilver's former six.
diet: Bite (Lv 20, its first move on evolving), Ice Fang (Lv 32) and Thrash point to a biting predator, but the moves name no food.
behavior: Once it appears it goes on a rampage, and stays enraged until it has demolished everything around it.
defense: Intimidate, its ability, lowers an opponent's Attack: few things will fight it at full strength.
habitat: Rarely seen in the wild; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by a Water-type move.
The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.

about: They have gentle hearts. Because they rarely fight, many have been caught. Their number has dwindled.

dossier.summary: A large, gentle sea animal that carries people across the water and has been hunted almost to extinction for its trouble. Lapras understands human speech, is said in one entry to read minds, and sings an enchanting cry when it is in a good mood; Hoenn's entries add that in the evenings it is said to sing plaintively, searching for the few others of its kind still left. Because it rarely fights, many were caught, and the games reflect that scarcity: in Johto a single Lapras surfaces in Union Cave, only on Fridays. Nothing in the Pokédex says what it eats.
senses: Intelligent enough to understand human speech.
behavior: Gentle and non-aggressive: they rarely fight.
social: It seeks out others of its kind: in the evenings it is said to sing plaintively, searching for the few that remain.
defense: Its gentleness is a liability: because it rarely fights, many have been caught.
habitat: The sea: it ferries people across it, and its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from paralysis.

about: It can transform into anything. When it sleeps, it changes into a stone to avoid being attacked.
senses: It has the ability to reconstitute its entire cellular structure to transform into whatever it sees.

dossier.summary: A small purple blob that can become anything. Ditto rearranges its whole cellular structure to transform into whatever it sees, copying an opponent's genetic code to become an almost perfect duplicate. The copy fails in two ways: if made to laugh it can't hold the disguise, and if it transforms from memory rather than sight it gets the details wrong. When it sleeps it turns into a stone so it won't be attacked, and when it meets another Ditto it hurries to copy it exactly. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 34 and 35, on Route 47 in swarms, and in Cerulean Cave by day.
diet: A Ditto that has become another species might eat as that species does while the copy lasts; nothing says so.
senses: It transforms into whatever it sees: sight drives the copy.
behavior: When it spots an enemy, its body transfigures into an almost perfect copy of its opponent.
social: Its one recorded interaction with its own kind is the race to copy: it duplicates another Ditto faster than normal.
defense: Disguise is its defence: it becomes a copy of its enemy, and a stone when it sleeps.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is urban; no entry describes where it lives.

abilities: Enables sure getaway from wild Pokémon.
Powers up moves of the same type.

about: It has the ability to alter the composition of its body to suit its surrounding environment.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by a Water-type move.

about: When Vaporeon's fins begin to vibrate, it is a sign that rain will come within a few hours.
moves: As it uses the fins on the tip of its tail to swim, it blends with the water perfectly.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by an Electric-type move.

about: It concentrates the weak electric charges emitted by its cells and launches wicked lightning bolts.

dossier.summary: Jolteon is the Thunder Stone form of Eevee, a 0.8 m, 24.5 kg Electric type that makes its own lightning. Its cells give off weak charges, which it concentrates and amplifies through the static of its fur to drop thunderbolts of 10,000 volts. When it is charged, angered or startled every hair stands up into sharp, charged needles that pierce attackers, and Platinum has it launching them in small bunches. A sensitive animal, it charges up with every change of mood, and its fur crackles constantly. Like every Eevee form it is never wild in Gen I–IV.
diet: It can take in electricity: Volt Absorb heals it when it is hit by an Electric move, and the Red, Blue and LeafGreen entries have it gathering negative ions from the atmosphere. That is energy uptake, but nothing shows it replaces food.
behavior: A sensitive animal that easily becomes sad or angry, and every change of mood charges it up.
social: An animal whose charge rises with its mood would be unpredictable company; close quarters with others of its kind, or with people, may keep it charged.
defense: If angered or startled, the fur all over its body bristles like sharp needles that pierce attackers.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: urban, the same as every Eevee form, which probably reflects where people get Eevee rather than a wild habitat.

abilities: It powers up Fire-type moves if it’s hit by one.

about: It stores some of the air it inhales in its internal flame pouch, which heats it to over 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

abilities: The Pokémon copies the foe’s ability.
Adjusts power according to the foe’s ability.

about: It is a manmade Pokémon. Since it doesn't breathe, people are eager to try it in any environment.
moves: The world’s first artificially created Pokémon. It can travel through electronic space.

The Pokémon is protected against critical hits.

about: Revived from an ancient fossil, this Pokémon uses air stored in its shell to sink and rise in water.
moves: A prehistoric Pokémon that lived in the primordial sea, it swims by twisting its 10 tentacles about.
defense: Revived from an ancient fossil, this Pokémon uses air stored in its shell to sink and rise in water.

defense: Apparently, it cracked Shellder's shell with its sharp fangs and sucked out the insides.

defense: It is thought to have inhabited beaches 300 million years ago. It is protected by a stiff shell.

moves: In the water, it tucks in its limbs to become more compact, then it wiggles its shell to swim fast.
defense: In the water, it tucks in its limbs to become more compact, then it wiggles its shell to swim fast.

moves: It was regenerated from a dinosaur’s genetic matter that was found in amber. It flies with high-pitched cries.
defense: A ferocious, prehistoric Pokémon that goes for the enemy’s throat with its serrated, sawlike fangs.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from getting poisoned.
Ups resistance to Fire-​ and Ice-type moves.

about: What sounds like its cry may actually be its snores or the rumblings of its hungry belly.
eats: Its stomach's digestive juices can dissolve any kind of poison. It can even eat things off the ground.
senses: It stops eating only to sleep. It doesn’t feel full unless it eats nearly 900 pounds a day.
defense: Its stomach's digestive juices can dissolve any kind of poison. It can even eat things off the ground.

dossier.summary: A 460 kg animal whose whole life is eating and sleeping. Snorlax is not satisfied until it has eaten roughly 400 kg of food a day, eats anything, moldy or rotten, off the ground if need be, and has a stomach that dissolves any poison; when it has eaten its fill it goes straight to sleep. It is so docile that children play on its belly, and Platinum notes that a full Snorlax is too lethargic to lift a finger. Its young, Munchlax, swallow their own weight in food every day and hide food under their long fur, then forget it is there.
diet: A generalist that eats anything, including moldy and rotten food and things off the ground.
senses: Satiety is its one described sense: it doesn't feel full until it has eaten nearly 900 pounds.
behavior: Its typical day is eating and sleeping and nothing else; when it has finished eating it goes promptly to sleep.
social: Docile toward people: children use its belly as a place to play.
defense: Bulk and indifference: little is described as threatening it, and it is too lethargic to react when full.
habitat: Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain; no entry describes where it lives.

abilities: The Pokémon raises the foe’s PP usage.

about: The magnificent, seemingly translucent wings of this legendary bird Pokémon are said to be made of ice.
moves: Legendary bird Pokémon. As it flies through the sky, it cools the air, causing snow to fall.

abilities: The Pokémon raises the foe’s PP usage.

about: This legendary bird Pokémon causes savage thunderstorms by flapping its glittering wings.

abilities: The Pokémon raises the foe’s PP usage.

about: This legendary Pokémon scatters embers with every flap of its wings. It is a thrilling sight to behold.
senses: This legendary Pokémon scatters embers with every flap of its wings. It is a thrilling sight to behold.

abilities: The Pokémon may heal its own status problems.

about: It is born large to start with. It repeatedly sheds its skin as it steadily grows longer.

dossier.summary: A long, very light water serpent that lives in Dragon's Den and a few other remote waters. Dratini is born large and grows by shedding its skin again and again; the entries put the constant moulting down to 'life energy' building up inside it. It was long thought to be mythical and is still called the Mirage Pokémon because so few people have seen one, though its shed skins turn up. No entry says what it eats, so its place in the den's food web is a gap, not a fact.
diet: Its first moves are Wrap and Leer (Lv 1) and Thunder Wave (Lv 5): a coiling grip and a paralysing jolt, the kit of an animal that holds and stuns prey rather than biting it.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Leer at Lv 1 is a stare, which suggests sight matters to it, but that is a reading of a move, not a description.
behavior: Rarely seen: it is called the Mirage Pokémon because so few have seen it, and its existence was only recently confirmed by a fisherman who caught one.
social: It was found as 'a small colony', so at least some Dratini live in groups.
defense: While it moults it is protected by a rapid waterfall, which implies the moult leaves it vulnerable and that fast water keeps attackers off.
habitat: An aquatic animal: a small colony was found living underwater, and Crystal places it under a rapid waterfall while it moults.

abilities: The Pokémon may heal its own status problems.

about: They say that if it emits an aura from its whole body, the weather will begin to change instantly.

dossier.summary: The middle stage of the Dratini line: a 4-metre serpent with crystal orbs on its neck and tail, said to change the weather around it by releasing stored energy through them. Much of what the Pokédex says about it is hedged with 'they say' and 'it is said', and the one first-hand account is a witness describing a strange aura, so it is the most folkloric animal in the highlands community. In HeartGold and SoulSilver the only wild ones are hooked by Super Rod in Dragon's Den and the Johto Safari Zone. As with Dratini, nothing says what it eats.
diet: Its level-up moves are Dratini's at later levels: Wrap, Thunder Wave, Slam, Aqua Tail (Lv 33), Dragon Rush (Lv 39). The same holding-and-stunning kit, on a much larger body.
defense: Shed Skin (it may heal its own status problems), the same as Dratini, and Safeguard at Lv 47.
habitat: It is said to live in seas and lakes.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from flinching.

about: It is said that this Pokémon constantly flies over the immense seas and rescues drowning people.
senses: Only a very few people ever see this Pokémon. Its intelligence is said to match that of humans.
moves: It is said that this Pokémon constantly flies over the immense seas and rescues drowning people.

dossier.summary: A bulky, winged sea dragon that most people never see. The Pokédex describes Dragonite flying over raging seas, circling the globe in sixteen hours, and leading lost ships to shore in storms; much of the rest of its record is rumour, including an island where only Dragonite live and an intelligence said to match ours. Its young are long, slender, skin-shedding Dratini, once thought mythical, which in Johto live in the Dragon's Den behind Blackthorn City. Nothing in any entry says what the line eats.
diet: In the Dragon's Den, the only other Pokémon in the water is Magikarp, which makes it the obvious candidate prey for Dratini and Dragonair there.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Finding lost ships in storms implies a good sense of direction and the ability to locate people in poor visibility.
behavior: A powerful long-distance flier: it can circle the globe in sixteen hours.
social: Dratini were found as a small colony living underwater, so the young live in groups.
defense: Nothing describes predators of Dragonite or how it defends itself; size, flight and rarity are its obvious protection.
habitat: Called a marine Pokémon, extremely rarely seen; its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is waters-edge.

abilities: The Pokémon raises the foe’s PP usage.

about: Because its battle abilities were raised to the ultimate level, it thinks only of defeating its foes.

abilities: Passes a burn, poison, or paralysis to the foe.

senses: Apparently, it appears only to those people who are pure of heart and have a strong desire to see it.

abilities: Powers up Grass-type moves in a pinch.

about: The scent of spices comes from around its neck. Somehow, sniffing it makes you want to fight.
senses: The scent of spices comes from around its neck. Somehow, sniffing it makes you want to fight.

about: The aroma that rises from its petals contains a substance that calms aggressive feelings.
senses: The fragrance of a Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, it gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.

dossier.summary: A large, sun-loving Grass Pokémon whose main tool is chemistry. The ring of petals around Meganium's neck gives off a scent that calms aggression, and in a fight it releases more of it to take the fight out of its opponent. Silver, SoulSilver and the Sinnoh Pokédex add that its breath can bring dead plants back to health. No entry says what it eats, and no game puts it in the wild: every Meganium starts as a Chikorita handed to a new trainer.
diet: The line probably gains some energy from sunlight: Chikorita loves to bask and sunbathe, and Synthesis, which restores health in sunlight, is a level-up move from Lv 12.
senses: Chikorita's head leaf senses temperature and humidity, and it uses it to seek out warm places.
behavior: The line is docile and loves to soak up the sun; Chikorita uses the leaf on its head to find warm places to bask.
social: Its scent works on other animals, so it communicates, or at least acts, chemically at close range: anyone standing beside it is refreshed.
defense: Chemical pacification rather than flight or armour: the flower's scent soothes, and it releases more in a fight. Chikorita does the same, waving its leaf to keep a foe back while the leaf's sweet scent calms everyone nearby.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex lists it under grassland.

abilities: Powers up Fire-type moves in a pinch.

about: It is timid and always curls itself up in a ball. If attacked, it flares up its back for protection.
defense: It flares flames from its back to protect itself. The fire burns vigorously if the Pokémon is angry. When it is tired, it sputters with incomplete combustion.

dossier.summary: A small, timid fire-backed animal that spends most of its time curled into a ball or hunched over, and shows its fire only when something frightens or angers it. The flames on its back are its whole defence: they flare when it is startled, burn hottest when it is angry, and sputter with incomplete combustion when it is tired, so its fire tells you its mood and its energy. No entry says what it eats or where a wild one lives; in every Johto game it comes from a professor in New Bark Town. It is the first stage of HeartGold's Typhlosion.
diet: The machine reading files it as a thermotroph only because it is a Fire type; nothing in the Pokédex says it takes in heat.
behavior: It is timid and always curls itself up in a ball.
defense: If attacked, it flares up its back for protection.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; no entry describes where it lives.

abilities: Powers up Fire-type moves in a pinch.

about: Be careful if it turns its back during battle. It means that it will attack with the fire on its back.

dossier.summary: The nimble middle stage of the Typhlosion line: a four-legged animal covered in nonflammable fur that keeps enemies off with the heat of its flames and gusts of superheated air, and dodges while it scorches. Before a fight it turns its back to show how fiercely its fire blazes, and a turned back is a warning that it is about to attack with that fire. Where Cyndaquil hides its fire until frightened, Quilava uses it on purpose. Nothing says what it eats, and it is never wild in any Gen I-IV game.
diet: The machine reading's thermotroph comes from its Fire type alone; the Pokédex never says it takes in heat.
behavior: Before battle, it turns its back on its opponent to demonstrate how ferociously its fire blazes.
defense: It keeps its foes at bay with the intensity of its flames and gusts of superheated air.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland. It is never found in the wild in any Gen I-IV game: it comes only from raising a Cyndaquil.

abilities: Powers up Fire-type moves in a pinch.

about: If its rage peaks, it becomes so hot that anything that touches it will instantly go up in flames.

dossier.summary: A large grassland animal with blazing fur that hides behind its own heat. Typhlosion makes the air around it shimmer with intense flame and conceals itself in the haze; when the shimmer rises it is ready to fight, and at the peak of its rage anything that touches it bursts into flame. Its young, Cyndaquil, are timid animals that curl into a ball and flare the fire on their backs only when startled, and whose flames sputter with incomplete combustion when they are tired. The Pokédex never says what the line eats, and no game has it in the wild.
diet: An animal that keeps a fire burning must eat a lot for its size, and a tired Cyndaquil's fire fails first, so food and flame are probably linked.
behavior: It hides behind a shimmering heat haze made with its own intense flames.
social: Its fire is readable by others: Cyndaquil's flames show anger and tiredness, Quilava's show readiness to fight, and Typhlosion's heat shimmer announces it. A line that signals its state with flame.
defense: At the peak of its rage it gets so hot that anything touching it instantly bursts into flames.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex lists the line under grassland; no entry describes where it lives.

abilities: Powers up Water-type moves in a pinch.

about: Its powerful, well-developed jaws are capable of crushing anything. Even its Trainer must be careful.
senses: This rough critter chomps at any moving object it sees. Turning your back on it is not recommended.

abilities: Powers up Water-type moves in a pinch.

about: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.
eats: The tips of its fangs are slanted backward. Once those fangs clamp down, the prey has no hope of escape.
defense: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.

abilities: Powers up Water-type moves in a pinch.

about: When it bites with its massive and powerful jaws, it shakes its head and savagely tears its victim up.
eats: It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.
moves: It opens its huge mouth to intimidate enemies. In battle, it runs using its thick and powerful hind legs to charge the foe with incredible speed.

dossier.summary: Feraligatr is the adult of the Big Jaw line: a 2.3 m, 89 kg predator of the water's edge, built around its bite. Most of the time it moves slowly; when it attacks it goes at blinding speed, clamps on and shakes its head to tear its victim apart. Out of water its weight is hard to carry, so it often drops to all fours, yet its thick hind legs can still launch a charge. No Gen I–IV game has a wild one: every Feraligatr in these games grew from a Totodile handed to a new trainer, so canon says nothing about where wild ones live or what they hunt.
diet: A predator: it bites prey, striking at blinding speed.
senses: Totodile chomps at any moving object it sees, which points to sight, and specifically sensitivity to movement, as the trigger for the line's strike.
behavior: Usually slow-moving, it switches to bursts of blinding speed when it attacks.
social: The juvenile nips at others in what it takes for play, which hints at play-biting with siblings or companions while young.
defense: Threat display: it opens its huge mouth to intimidate foes.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex files the whole line under the water's edge.

senses: It stands on its tail so it can see a long way. If it spots an enemy, it cries loudly to warn its kind.

about: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

dossier.summary: A small owl with a perfect sense of time. Hoothoot stands on one foot, switching feet too fast to see, and begins to hoot at precisely the same time every day, thanks to an internal organ that tracks the Earth's rotation; some trainers use it as a clock. No entry says what it eats or when it is active, but HeartGold and SoulSilver meet it in grass only at night, and in Ilex Forest it is the animal most often shaken out of the Headbutt trees.
diet: Its evolved form catches prey in darkness, and Hoothoot's own moves include Peck (Lv 9) and Foresight (Lv 1), so it is most likely a small predator.
senses: A perfect sense of time, from an organ that senses the Earth's rotation.
behavior: It begins to hoot at precisely the same time every day.
social: Nothing is said about groups or pairs. Its daily hoot at a fixed time might be a signal to others, but no entry says who hears it.
defense: Even when attacked it doesn't brace itself on both feet.
habitat: A forest animal. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's common (60%) and rare (50%) Headbutt trees, in Headbutt trees across Johto from New Bark Town to Ecruteak City, and in grass at night on Routes 29 to 31 and 35 to 37 and in National Park.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from falling asleep.
Prevents the Pokémon from losing accuracy.

about: Its eyes are specially adapted. They concentrate even faint light and enable it to see in the dark.
eats: Its extremely soft feathers make no sound in flight. It silently sneaks up on prey without being detected.
senses: Its eyes are specially adapted. They concentrate even faint light and enable it to see in the dark.

dossier.summary: The adult of Hoothoot and Ilex Forest's night hunter. Noctowl's eyes concentrate faint light so it can see in near darkness, and its soft feathers make no sound in flight, so it reaches prey unheard; the entries say it never fails to catch prey in the dark. When it thinks hard it turns its head 180 degrees, or upside down. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in Ilex Forest's rarer Headbutt trees, and it is the community's best candidate for a top predator.
diet: A predator: it sneaks silently up on prey and never fails to catch prey in darkness.
senses: Superior night vision: it can pick out objects with the tiniest amount of light and see clearly in murky darkness.
behavior: A night hunter: its entries are about catching prey in darkness, and every grass record of it in HeartGold and SoulSilver is at night.
defense: No entry describes a defence. Its size probably suffices in Ilex Forest, where only Golduck is larger.
habitat: A forest animal. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is in Ilex Forest's rare Headbutt trees (10%) and Viridian Forest's, and in grass at night on Routes 2, 8, 13 to 15, 43 and 47.

abilities: Powers up Bug-type moves in a pinch.
The Pokémon awakens quickly from sleep.

about: It is very timid. It will be afraid to move if it is alone. But it will be active if it is in a group.
senses: It is so timid, it can’t move if it isn’t with a swarm of others. It conveys its feelings with scent.

dossier.summary: A timid red beetle that can't bring itself to move alone: on its own it is afraid to move, but in a group it becomes active. Ledyba talk to each other by scent, through an aromatic fluid they secrete where their legs join the body, changing the smell to convey their feelings; the fluid also marks where they have been. When the weather turns cold, Ledyba gather from everywhere into clusters to keep each other warm. Nothing says what it eats. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is a SoulSilver Pokémon: in the morning grass of a few routes, and in headbutt trees almost everywhere, Viridian Forest included.
diet: Bug Bite is an egg move of its line and Comet Punch and Mach Punch are in its own list: it punches more than it bites, which says nothing about food.
senses: Scent is its social sense: it reads feelings in the fluid's smell.
behavior: It is very timid: it will be afraid to move if it is alone, but it will be active in a group.
defense: Safety in numbers: alone it won't move at all.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

abilities: Powers up Bug-type moves in a pinch.
The Pokémon awakens quickly from sleep.

about: When the stars flicker in the night sky, it flutters about, scattering a glowing powder.

dossier.summary: The adult of Ledyba, a night-flying beetle that lives on starlight. Ledian uses the light of the stars as its energy, and the star or spot patterns on its back grow larger or smaller with the number of stars in the night sky. When the stars flicker it flutters about scattering a glowing powder; on warm days it curls up inside a big leaf and sleeps deeply. It is said to live in countless numbers in lands with clean air where the stars fill the sky. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is SoulSilver's: on Route 2 in the morning and in the trees of Viridian Forest.
diet: It uses the light of the stars as its energy.
senses: It responds to the stars: its patterns and its flight follow their number and flicker, so it senses faint night light.
behavior: When the stars flicker in the night sky, it flutters about, scattering a glowing powder.
social: It is said to live in countless numbers where the stars fill the sky; its young can't move without a swarm (165.7).
defense: Nothing in its entries describes defence; it keeps its young's screens (Light Screen, Reflect, Safeguard) and fights with Comet Punch and Mach Punch.
habitat: Lands with clean air where the stars fill the sky are said to hold Ledian in countless numbers; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

abilities: Powers up Bug-type moves in a pinch.
Prevents the Pokémon from falling asleep.

about: It lies still in the same pose for days in its web, waiting for its unsuspecting prey to wander close.
eats: It lies still in the same pose for days in its web, waiting for its unsuspecting prey to wander close.
senses: The web it spins can be considered its second nervous system. It is said that a Spinarak determines its prey by the tiny vibrations it feels through the web.

dossier.summary: A small green web-spinning spider and a sit-and-wait predator. Spinarak spins a web of fine but durable thread, then lies still in the same pose for days, waiting for unsuspecting prey to wander close; if prey gets caught, it waits motionless until dark. Its web is said to work as a second nervous system: through the tiny vibrations in the strands it can tell what kind of prey is touching it. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: walking at night on a few routes and in the headbutt trees of nearly every wooded place, Viridian Forest among them.
diet: It sets a trap by spinning a web, then waits patiently, motionless, for prey to be trapped or to arrive.
senses: The web can be considered its second nervous system.
behavior: A sit-and-wait predator: still for days in the same pose.
social: Nothing is said about Spinarak together; every entry is about a single spider on its web.
defense: Nothing in its entries describes defence. Its moves include Scary Face (Lv 5), Constrict, Night Shade and Shadow Sneak, and as a Poison type its sting carries venom.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest; its web is its nest ('its nest of spun string').

abilities: Powers up Bug-type moves in a pinch.
Prevents the Pokémon from falling asleep.

about: It spins string not only from its rear but also from its mouth. It’s hard to tell which end is which.
eats: It attaches silk to its prey and sets it free. Later, it tracks the silk to the prey and its friends.
defense: Its feet are tipped with tiny hooked claws that enable it to scuttle on ceilings and vertical walls. It constricts its foe with thin and strong silk webbing.

dossier.summary: The adult of Spinarak, a long-legged red spider that gives up the web for the hunt. Ariados doesn't keep a nest in one spot: it wanders in search of food after dark. It spins string from both its rear and its mouth, so it is hard to tell which end is which, and it has a trick no other spider in the Pokédex has: it attaches silk to its prey, lets it go, and later follows the thread back to the prey and its friends. Hooked claws let it run on walls and ceilings, and it constricts its foes in silk. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is HeartGold's: on Route 2 at night and in Viridian Forest's trees.
diet: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, rather than keeping a nest in one spot.
senses: It tracks prey by following its own silk: a sense of touch along the thread, inherited from Spinarak's web-reading (167.4).
behavior: Nocturnal: it hunts after darkness falls, and HeartGold has it walking on Route 2 only at night.
defense: It constricts the foe with thin and strong silk webbing.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest. A single strand of special string is endlessly spun from its rear and leads back to its nest (Silver, SoulSilver), though Crystal says it keeps no nest in one spot.

abilities: The Pokémon is protected from flinching.

about: It flies so silently through the dark on its four wings that it may not be noticed even when nearby.
eats: Crobat sneaks up on its intended prey using wings that barely make a sound. This Pokémon rests by hanging on a tree branch with its rear legs that serve as wings.
moves: It flies so silently through the dark on its four wings that it may not be noticed even when nearby.

dossier.summary: A four-winged bat whose hind legs have become a second pair of wings, built for fast, nearly silent flight in the dark. Crobat sneaks up on prey on wings that barely make a sound, and on long flights it rests one pair while flying on the other. Its line is the most familiar night animal of Johto's caves: eyeless, echolocating Zubat that roost by day and avoid sunlight, and Golbat, which drink the blood of people and Pokémon and are common in the Ice Path next to Blackthorn. Crobat itself is never wild; it comes only from a Golbat that is close to its trainer.
diet: Crobat hunts by stealth: it sneaks up on its intended prey with wings that barely make a sound. The prey is not named.
senses: Echolocation: Zubat emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth and reads their reflections to find its way and detect obstacles and targets.
behavior: Nocturnal: Crobat turns active when night comes; Golbat is most active in pitch-black, moonless nights; Zubat sleeps until sundown.
social: Zubat are colonial: they gather by day and hang from the ceilings of caves and old buildings.
defense: Silence and darkness are its cover; no entry describes predators of the line.
habitat: Caves and dark places: Zubat forms colonies in perpetually dark places and roosts by day in caves, old buildings and deep forest. Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by an Electric-type move.

about: It shoots positive and negative electricity between the tips of its two antennae and zaps its enemies.
eats: Chinchou lets loose positive and negative electrical charges from its two antennas to make its prey faint. This Pokémon flashes its electric lights to exchange signals with others.
senses: When it senses danger, it discharges positive and negative electricity from its two antennae. It lives in depths beyond sunlight’s reach.

dossier.summary: A small electric fish of the dark ocean floor, in depths beyond sunlight's reach. Chinchou's two antennae, which evolved from a fin, are filled with cells that make so much electricity it tingles itself; it shoots positive and negative charges between their tips to make prey faint and to shock its foes. On the dark sea floor its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights, which it uses to exchange signals with others. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the good and super rods along both regions' coasts, from New Bark Town and Sea Route 41 to Pallet Town, Vermilion and the seas around Cinnabar.
diet: A hunter: it lets loose positive and negative charges from its antennae to make its prey faint.
senses: It senses danger, and discharges when it does; how is not said.
social: On the dark ocean floor its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights; it flashes them to exchange signals with others.
defense: It shoots electricity between its antenna tips and zaps its enemies; when it senses danger, it discharges positive and negative electricity.
habitat: The dark ocean floor, in depths beyond sunlight's reach; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Restores HP if hit by an Electric-type move.

about: The light it emits is so bright that it can illuminate the sea's surface from a depth of over three miles.
eats: It blinds prey with an intense burst of light. With the prey incapacitated, the Pokémon swallows it in a single gulp.
senses: Lanturn is known to emit light. If you peer down into the dark sea from a ship at night, you can sometimes see this Pokémon’s light rising from the depths where it swims. It gives the sea an appearance of a starlit night.
moves: Lanturn is known to emit light. If you peer down into the dark sea from a ship at night, you can sometimes see this Pokémon’s light rising from the depths where it swims. It gives the sea an appearance of a starlit night.

dossier.summary: The adult of Chinchou, nicknamed 'the deep-sea star'. Lanturn makes light by a chemical reaction between bacteria and its body fluids inside its antenna, a part changed from its dorsal fin; the light is so bright it can illuminate the sea's surface from more than three miles down. It uses the bright part of its body to lure prey, then blinds the prey with an intense burst of light and swallows it, immobilized, in a single gulp. From a ship at night you can sometimes see its light rising from the depths, making the sea look like a starlit night. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is hooked on the super rod at the same coasts as Chinchou in both regions.
diet: It lures prey with the bright part of its body, blinds it with an intense burst of light, and swallows the immobilized prey in a single gulp.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. A hunter that lights its own prey can see by its own light.
behavior: It sometimes rises from the depths where it swims; from a ship at night its light can be seen coming up.
defense: The burst of light that blinds prey would blind a predator too.
habitat: The inky darkness of deep seas, from great depths; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is sea.

abilities: Contact with the Pokémon may cause paralysis.

about: It is not yet skilled at storing electricity. It may send out a jolt if amused or startled.
senses: Pichu charges itself with electricity more easily on days with thunderclouds or when the air is very dry. You can hear the crackling of static electricity coming off this Pokémon.

dossier.summary: The young of Pikachu, a tiny electric mouse (0.3 m, 2.0 kg) that hasn't yet learned to hold its charge. Its cheek pouches are small and can't store much, so any shock, fright or even amusement makes it discharge, and the jolt surprises Pichu as much as anyone; it gets better at holding power as it grows. Young Pichu play by touching tails and setting off sparks, a test of courage that can end in tears when the sparks flash. It charges more easily in thundery or very dry weather. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is never wild; Crystal gives it as an egg, and only Sinnoh's Trophy Garden has it wild.
diet: The adult gathers Berries and softens hard ones with electricity (Pikachu's dossier), so the young most likely eats fruit too, but this is the adult's diet, not Pichu's.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. It is startled by flashes of its own sparks, so it sees them.
behavior: It may send out a jolt if amused or startled; any kind of shock makes it discharge spontaneously.
social: Young Pichu play together. When one shorts out its electricity with another, it makes a shower of sparks and the Pichu begins to cry, startled by the flash.
defense: Its electricity is a defence it can't yet control: it zaps when startled, even adult humans, despite its size.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

senses: Igglybuff has a soft and plushy body that feels very much like a marshmallow. From this body wafts a gently sweet fragrance that soothes and calms the emotions of its foes.

senses: It runs up short trees that grow on the savanna to peck at new shoots. A Natu’s eyes look as if they are always observing something.
moves: It runs up short trees that grow on the savanna to peck at new shoots. A Natu’s eyes look as if they are always observing something.

dossier.summary: Ampharos is the light-bearer of the Wool line: the tip of its tail shines brightly enough to be seen far away, over open sea at night, and people have treasured it as a beacon since ancient times, using it to send signals and to guide the lost. Its electricity begins in the young: Mareep's fleece builds static as the wool rubs together, and the more charge it holds, the brighter its tail glows. Flaaffy grows a rubbery, insulated hide and loses patches of wool to the charge it stores. Ampharos itself is never found wild in Gen I–IV, so everything about its wild life is read through Mareep and Flaaffy on Johto's grassy routes.
diet: A woolly grassland quadruped as a juvenile, it plausibly grazes; its electricity is described as made by friction in its wool, not taken in from outside, so it isn't fed by electricity.
senses: Mareep's lineage can carry Odor Sleuth as an egg move, a hint that smell matters to some lines, but it is not a natural move of Ampharos.
behavior: Mareep is on the Route 32 and 43 tables morning, day and night, at a lower rate at night; Ampharos's light is noticed 'when it gets dark'. It seems to be about by day and night alike.
social: A light visible from far off, carried by a grassland animal, could serve to keep a scattered group in contact at night; nothing in canon says Ampharos signal to each other.
defense: Static: touching any stage risks a shock, and in the games contact may paralyse.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat for every stage: grassland.

senses: Marill’s oil-filled tail acts much like a life preserver. If you see just its tail bobbing on the water’s surface, it’s a sure indication that this Pokémon is diving beneath the water to feed on aquatic plants.

moves: It can be carried away on even the gentlest breeze. It may even float all the way to the next town.

dossier.summary: A tiny pink plant-like Pokémon so light (0.5 kg) that it drifts on the wind. Hoppip must grip the ground firmly with its feet to keep from being blown away, and can be carried off by the gentlest breeze, even all the way to the next town. When it senses strong winds coming, it links its leaves with other Hoppip so they cling together, and they gather in clusters against the wind, though they enjoy gentle breezes. It is said that when Hoppip gather in fields and mountains, spring is on the way. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives by day on Routes 32, 33 and 48 in Johto and Routes 13, 14 and 15 in Kanto.
diet: Synthesis (Lv 4) is a sunlight-healing move and Chlorophyll speeds it in sunshine: in game terms a sun-dependent plant, so it most likely lives on sunlight as plants do.
senses: It senses the approach of strong winds.
behavior: It drifts and floats with the wind; it can be carried away on even the gentlest breeze.
social: To keep from being blown away by the wind, they gather in clusters.
defense: Its powders are its defences: Poison Powder (Lv 12), Stun Spore (Lv 14), Sleep Powder (Lv 16) and Cotton Spore (Lv 28). Leaf Guard keeps off status in sun.
habitat: Fields and mountains, where it gathers in spring by the saying; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland.

dossier.summary: A long-tailed tree-dweller that lives high among the treetops of tall and giant trees. Aipom's tail ends in a dexterous, hand-like appendage, strong enough to grab a branch and hold it up in the air; it balances with it as it leaps, swings from branch to branch on it, wraps it round a branch so it won't fall while asleep, and plucks fruits out of reach with it. It uses the tail so much its real hands have become clumsy. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the trees, shaken out by Headbutt, on Johto's Routes 33, 42, 44, 45 and 46 and at Azalea Town, and up on Route 28 and Mt. Silver.
diet: It uses its tail to pluck fruits that are out of reach.
behavior: When leaping from branch to branch, it deftly uses its tail for balance; it uses its momentum to swing from one branch to another.
social: Nothing is said about Aipom living together. Its adult works in large colonies and links tails with others, apparently in friendship, said to be a way of talking (424.2, 424.4).
defense: It lives high in the trees, out of reach.
habitat: It lives atop tall trees, giant trees, high among the treetops; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

eats: It lives by drinking only dewdrops from under the leaves of plants. It is said that it eats nothing else.

senses: Its large eyes can scan 360 degrees. It looks in all directions to seek out insects as its prey.
