moves: Due to its relaxed and carefree attitude, it often bumps its head on boulders and boat hulls as it swims.

dossier.summary: Espeon is the day form of Eevee, a 0.9 m, 26.5 kg Psychic type whose coat works as a sense organ. Its fine, velvety fur feels minute shifts in the air, and by reading air currents it predicts the weather and an opponent's next move; the tip of its forked tail quivers as it does. It is extremely loyal to any trainer it judges worthy, and it is said its foresight developed to protect that person. No Espeon is wild in Gen I–IV: the games make it only from an Eevee that is devoted to its trainer and levels up by day.
diet: Its category is the Sun Pokémon and it learns Morning Sun (Lv 71), which restores health in sunlight; sunlight may matter to its energy budget, but nothing says it lives on light.
senses: Its main sense is touch through the fur: it feels minute shifts in the air.
behavior: By reading air currents it predicts its foe's next move, and the weather.
social: It is extremely loyal to any trainer it considers worthy, which means it judges people and doesn't bond with just anyone.
defense: Early warning: its fur senses air currents so it can anticipate an enemy's actions.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: urban, the same as every Eevee form, which probably reflects where people get Eevee rather than a wild habitat.

abilities: Passes a burn, poison, or paralysis to the foe.

eats: The light of the moon changed Eevee’s genetic structure. It lurks in darkness for prey.

dossier.summary: Umbreon is the night form of Eevee: a 1 m, 27 kg Dark-type ambusher that hides silently in darkness and waits for prey or foes to move first. The rings on its body glow yellow after dark, on full-moon nights, when it is excited and as it leaps, and the glow strikes fear in anyone nearby. When agitated it sprays poisonous sweat from its pores. The entries credit its origin to moonlight changing Eevee's genes; the games make it from an Eevee that is devoted to its trainer and levels up at night, and no Umbreon is wild in any Gen I–IV game.
diet: A predator: it lurks in darkness for prey.
senses: No entry describes its senses. An ambusher that waits in darkness for prey to move must detect movement in low light, by sight, hearing or both.
behavior: A sit-and-wait ambusher: it hides silently in darkness, waits for its foe to make a move, and leaps to attack.
social: It keeps Helping Hand from Eevee at Lv 1, the only hint of cooperation in its repertoire; no entry describes Umbreon helping one another.
defense: When agitated it protects itself by spraying poisonous sweat from its pores.
habitat: It lives and hunts in darkness.

Heightens the critical- hit ratios of moves.

about: Feared and loathed by many, it is believed to bring misfortune to all those who see it at night.
senses: Feared and loathed by many, it is believed to bring misfortune to all those who see it at night.
moves: It appears near travelers to lure them into deep forests. It is said to carry misfortune.

abilities: Prevents the Pokémon from becoming confused.

about: It has incredible intellect and intuition. Whatever the situation, it remains calm and collected.
defense: Every time it yawns, Shellder injects more poison into it. The poison makes it more intelligent.

senses: It loves to bite and yank people's hair from behind without warning, just to see their shocked reactions.

senses: If two or more Wobbuffet meet, they will turn competitive and try to outdo each other’s endurance. However, they may try to see which one can endure the longest without food. TrainerS need to beware of this habit.

dossier.summary: A patient blue cave dweller that never attacks first and puts everything into enduring blows and returning them. It keeps its black tail hidden in the dark, comes out only at night, and fights ferociously only when the tail is attacked, when it may try to take the attacker down with it. Its young, Wynaut, love sweet fruit and gather in fruit gardens, but no entry says what an adult eats; Wobbuffet that meet are even said to compete over who can go longest without food. In the highlands it lives only at the Blackthorn end of Dark Cave.
diet: Its young, Wynaut, love sweet fruit, which they pick with their earlike arms; they gather in fruit gardens, drawn by the fragrance.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Hating light suggests eyes, or skin, adapted to the dark.
behavior: It is never first to attack and does nothing but endure attacks; it is usually docile.
social: If two or more Wobbuffet meet, they turn competitive and try to outdo each other's endurance, even in going without food. Trainers are warned to beware of this habit.
defense: It will not endure an attack on its tail: then it strikes back ferociously and tries to take the foe with it using Destiny Bond.
habitat: It lives quietly in darkness, in a dark cave, and makes its lair in caves where it waits for nightfall.

about: Its tail has a small brain of its own. Beware! If you get close, it may react to your scent by biting.
eats: A Girafarig is an herbivore--it eats grass and tree shoots. While it is eating, its tail makes chewing and swallowing motions as if it were also eating.
senses: Its tail has a small brain of its own. Beware! If you get close, it may react to your scent by biting.

about: It likes to make its shell thicker by adding layers of tree bark. The additional weight doesn't bother it.

defense: It likes to make its shell thicker by adding layers of tree bark. The additional weight doesn't bother it.

dossier.summary: A sit-and-wait predator of the forest canopy that builds its own armour. Pineco hangs from a branch inside a case of tree bark it glues on with a fluid that sets in air, waits for flying insects to come close, and barely moves otherwise. It passes for a pinecone, which keeps birds from treating it as food; if its tree is shaken while it feeds it drops and explodes. In Johto it lives in the trees themselves: every wild Pineco in the Johto games is found by shaking a tree.
diet: It eats flying insects, which it waits for rather than chases.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. An ambush predator of flying insects must detect prey approaching through the air, so vision or vibration sense is implied but not described; as Forretress its eyes are the only part visible through the shell.
behavior: Sedentary: it doesn't move about much on its own.
social: No entry describes groups, pairs or interaction with its own kind; the sedentary ambush life suggests it lives alone on its branch.
defense: Masquerade: it looks just like a pinecone, and its shell protects it from bird Pokémon that peck it by mistake.
habitat: A forest animal that lives in trees, hanging from branches.

abilities: It is protected against 1-hit KO attacks.

about: Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.
eats: It keeps itself inside its steel shell. The shell is opened when it is catching prey, but it is so quick that the shell’s inside cannot be seen.
senses: It is encased in a steel shell. Its peering eyes are all that can be seen of its mysterious innards.
defense: Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.

abilities: Boosts the likelihood of added effects appearing.

dossier.summary: A 1.5-metre 'land snake' with a drill-tipped tail and small wings. The moment it is spotted it bores backwards into the ground with its tail; the wings let it float or fly just a little. It hides deep in caves where no light reaches, stays almost motionless, and digs complex, maze-like nests deep underground. Nothing says what it eats. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives at the Violet City end of Dark Cave, nearly always found by smashing rocks, and not at the Blackthorn end.
diet: Its early level-up moves immobilise rather than wound, Yawn (Lv 9) and Glare (Lv 13), and Pursuit (Lv 25) hits a fleeing target. If it eats animals, the kit fits taking slow or fleeing small prey.
senses: Living where no light ever reaches, it can't rely on sight there; how it senses its surroundings is not described.
behavior: When spotted, it escapes backward by furiously boring into the ground with its tail.
defense: Escape by burrowing is its defence; Run Away (a sure getaway from wild Pokémon) is the game form of it. Its other ability is Serene Grace.
habitat: It hides deep inside caves where no light ever reaches.

dossier.summary: A gliding scorpion of cliffs. Gligar usually clings to cliff faces and builds its nest on a steep one; when it spots prey it spreads its wings and glides down without a sound, as if sliding, flies straight at the prey's face, clamps on with its clawed hind legs and the big pincers on its forelegs, and injects poison with its barb. Done gliding, it hops along the ground back to its nest. In HeartGold it lives on Route 45, the steep mountain road south of Blackthorn; it is not in SoulSilver's wild.
diet: A hunter: when it spots prey it glides down to attack, aiming for the prey's face, and injects the prey with its poison barb.
senses: It spots prey from the cliff before it glides: sight from a height.
behavior: It glides without making a single sound, as if it were sliding, sailing on the winds with its limbs extended.
social: Nothing is said about Gligar living together. It builds a nest, so it has a home place.
defense: It flies straight at a target's face and clamps down on the startled victim to inject poison; it startles foes by clamping on to their faces.
habitat: Cliffs: it usually clings to them and builds its nest on a steep cliff. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.

senses: It chews its way through boulders with its sturdy jaws. Its eyes can see in the darkness underground.
moves: Steelix live even further underground than Onix. This Pokémon is known to dig toward the earth’s core, reaching a depth of over six-tenths of a mile underground.

dossier.summary: A steel-hard, red insect that has traded its parent's camouflage and flight for armour and a bluff. Scizor's pincers carry eye-like markings that it raises to make itself look three-headed, and they contain steel enough to crush any hard object. Its wings no longer fly; it flaps them fast to regulate its body temperature. It develops from Scyther, a green, grass-hiding ambusher with scythes that cut logs, and in the games only a Scyther traded while holding a Metal Coat becomes one.
diet: Scyther is a predator: it leaps out of tall grass to slice prey, and tears and shreds it with its scythes.
senses: Nothing is said about Scizor's senses. An eyespot display only works on predators that see well, so its enemies are probably visual hunters.
behavior: Threat display: it raises its eye-patterned pincers to intimidate, which makes it look three-headed, and it can swing them down dangerously.
social: No entry describes groups. Scyther's speed can create the illusion of more than one, which is a solitary animal looking like many, not a group.
defense: A deimatic bluff: the eyespots on its raised pincers make it look like a three-headed animal.
habitat: Its Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is grassland; Scyther hides in tall grass.

dossier.summary: A great horned beetle, clad in a steel-hard shell, that gathers in forests seeking the sweet sap of trees, its favourite food, and loves sweet honey. Usually docile, it chases off anyone who disturbs it while it sips, and hurls rivals away with its prized horn to keep the honey to itself: it charges, slips under a foe, and scoops up and flings it, with power enough to throw 100 times its own weight or topple a massive tree. Clawed feet planted in the ground or in bark give it footing. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives in the trees, shaken out by Headbutt, on Johto's Routes 33, 42, 44, 45, 46 and 47, at Azalea Town and on Mt. Silver, and in Kanto on Route 28, at Vermilion and Celadon, and on Routes 7, 11 and 16.
diet: Tree sap is its favourite food; Heracross gather in forests seeking the sweet sap of trees.
behavior: It is usually docile, but if it is disturbed while sipping honey it chases off the intruder with its horn.
social: Heracross gather in forests at sap trees: a feeding gathering.
defense: A steel-hard shell, and the horn: it throws foes over great distances.
habitat: Forests, where it gathers at sap trees; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.

dossier.summary: A little bear that always licks its paws, because they are soaked with honey; every set of paws tastes unique. When it finds honey its crescent mark glows, and it makes its own honey by blending fruits with pollen that Beedrill collected. Before food becomes scarce in winter it hoards food in many hidden places. It grows into Ursaring, a forest bear that snaps trees to eat the berries that fall and can smell food buried deep underground. In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45, the mountain road below Blackthorn, and on Mt. Silver; in HeartGold, Phanpy has its place.
diet: Honey: it always licks it, letting it soak into its paws so it can lick them all the time.
senses: It finds honey, and its mark glows when it does; how it finds it is not said. Its adult can distinguish any aroma (217.2).
behavior: It always licks its honey-soaked paws.
social: Nothing is said about Teddiursa living together. Its adult leaves scratches on trees in its territory (217.8), so the line keeps territories.
defense: Fake Tears, Charm (Lv 36) and Feint Attack (Lv 15): it disarms and tricks rather than fights; Fury Swipes (Lv 8) and Slash are its claws.
habitat: No entry says where it lives; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.

dossier.summary: A lava snail whose shell is its own skin, cooled and hardened, and so brittle it crumbles at a touch; flames escape through the gaps. Its entries give a body temperature of about 18,000°F, a figure hard to square with a shell that is simply cooled skin. No game puts Magcargo or its young form Slugma anywhere near Blackthorn, so its place in the highlands community is Blackthorn's own choice: a possible heat source in a frozen, energy-poor landscape, and a test of whether hot ground exists there at all. Swinub's habit of rooting out hot springs is the only canon hint that it might.
diet: It returns to its original size by dipping itself in magma, so magma restores its body.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Slugma's constant search for warm places implies it can sense heat.
behavior: Slugma never sleeps: it has to keep moving because if it stopped, its magma body would cool and harden. The Magcargo entries don't say whether the adult shares this.
social: Slugma group together in places hotter than normal: aggregations at heat, not necessarily social bonds.
defense: Flame Body (contact may burn the attacker) and Magma Armor (it can't be frozen); in the highlands the second matters as much as the first.
habitat: Volcanic craters, where Magcargo have lived for tens of thousands of years; Slugma are a common sight in volcanic areas.

about: It rubs its snout on the ground to find and dig up food. It sometimes discovers hot springs.

moves: It rubs its snout on the ground to find and dig up food. It sometimes discovers hot springs.

dossier.summary: A small pig of the Ice Path that finds food by smell and digs it up with a nose tough enough for frozen ground. Its favourite food is a mushroom that grows under dead grass, and it also eats berries, which makes it the highlands' clearest link to the fungi that break down dead plants. While rooting it sometimes uncovers hot springs, even under ice. It has the highest encounter rate on every floor of the Ice Path in HeartGold and SoulSilver, which says it is easy to meet, not how many there are.
diet: Its favourite food is a mushroom that grows under the cover of dead or dried grass.
senses: Smell is its main sense: a very sensitive nose that leads it to food, and to hot springs, even under ice.
behavior: If it smells something enticing, it dashes off headlong to find the source.
defense: Snow Cloak raises its evasion in a hailstorm: in the games it is harder to hit in blowing snow.
habitat: In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is on all four floors of the Ice Path (1F, B1F, B2F, B3F) at 40%, the highest rate there, at any time of day; levels 21-23 on the upper floors and 22-24 on B2F and B3F. Gold and Silver have the same 40% at every time of day; Crystal has it only by day and morning.

about: Because the long hair all over its body obscures its sight, it just keeps charging repeatedly.
eats: A Piloswine is covered by a thick coat of long hair for enduring freezing cold. It uses its tusks to dig up food that has been buried under ice.
senses: Because the long hair all over its body obscures its sight, it just keeps charging repeatedly.
moves: A Piloswine is covered by a thick coat of long hair for enduring freezing cold. It uses its tusks to dig up food that has been buried under ice.

dossier.summary: The shaggy middle stage of the Swinub line: a short-legged, long-haired swine built for freezing cold, with rugged hooves that don't slip on ice and tusks it uses to dig up food buried under ice. Its coat covers its eyes, so it finds its way by a sensitive nose and very sensitive hearing, and when it charges it simply keeps charging, hair standing up on its back. Its tusks of ice thicken when it snows. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it is never wild: it comes only from raising a Swinub, which lives in the Ice Path.
diet: It uses its tusks to dig up food that has been buried under ice.
senses: Its shaggy coat leaves it unable to see; it checks its surroundings with its sensitive nose instead.
behavior: Because the long hair all over its body obscures its sight, it just keeps charging repeatedly.
social: Oblivious, one of its abilities, keeps it from becoming infatuated: in game terms it is hard to charm.
defense: Its defence is the charge: it keeps charging, hair raised, at whatever threatens it.
habitat: Cold places: its coat endures freezing cold, its hooves grip ice, and the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is cave.

dossier.summary: A cliff-nesting bird of cold mountains that carries its food bundled in its tail wherever it goes, ferries it to its chicks all day, and throws it at anything that attacks. Several entries add that it shares that food with people lost in the mountains, and tell of an explorer who reached the top of Mt. Everest thanks to one; the tales are kept under folklore here. No entry says what the food actually is. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only in SoulSilver's Ice Path.
diet: It carries food all day long and always has it with it, wherever it goes.
behavior: It spends all day carrying food to its waiting chicks.
social: Parents provision their chicks at the nest.
defense: If attacked, it throws its food at the opponent.
habitat: It nests at the edge of sharp cliffs, in the mountains.

dossier.summary: An armoured bird with a body and wings of steel. Its sturdy wings look heavy but its bones are hollow and light, and it flies at over 180 mph, slashing foes with wings that have sword-like cutting edges. It nests in bramble bushes, and its chicks' wings grow hard from the scratches of the thorns. Its wings are battered by battles and grow back completely once a year. The feathers it sheds are very sharp: people in the past made swords and knives from them. In SoulSilver it lives on Route 45, the mountain road below Blackthorn, rarely; in HeartGold, Gligar has its place.
diet: The machine reading's metal-eater comes from its Steel type alone; nothing supports it.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Keen Eye, its ability, is a game reading of sharp sight.

social: Nothing is said about Skarmory living together. It raises chicks in a nest.
defense: Its armour, and wings that cut like swords.
habitat: It nests in bramble bushes; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

dossier.summary: A black, horned hound of rough country and the rival's FireRed Pokémon. Houndoom lives in packs led by the one whose horns rake sharply back, and the pack chooses its leader by fighting. Its flame is made by toxins burning in its body: it smells pungent, and a burn from it is said to hurt forever. Its eerie howl sends other Pokémon shivering back to their nests, and people long ago imagined it was the call of the grim reaper. Its young, Houndour, are cooperative pack hunters that corner prey with barks only they understand. In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Houndoom is found only in the Johto Safari Zone; Houndour lives on Kanto's Route 7 at night.
diet: Its young hunt as a coordinated pack and corner prey with barks only they understand (228.2, 228.4), so the line is a pack predator.
senses: Nothing is said about its own senses. Odor Sleuth and its young's bark-based teamwork suggest a nose and ears for hunting.
behavior: Upon hearing its eerie howls, other Pokémon get the shivers and head straight back to their nests.
social: It lives in packs; the one with its horns raked sharply back serves as leader, and they choose their leader by fighting among themselves.
defense: Its flame's burn is said to hurt forever: if you are burned by it, the pain will never go away.
habitat: The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

dossier.summary: The adult of the Horsea line, and the rival's Crystal Pokémon: a 152 kg sea dragon that sleeps on the deepest sea floor, at depths where nothing else can survive, to build up its energy. When it moves it makes whirlpools, giant enough to swallow ships when it comes to the surface. Much of what is told of it is told as belief: that it hides in underwater caves, that its yawning makes spiralling ocean currents, that it causes tornadoes as it wakes, and that it wakes with storms to wander in search of prey. It is never wild in a Gen I-IV game: it comes only from trading a Seadra that holds a Dragon Scale.
diet: When a storm arrives, it is said to awaken and wander about in search of prey.
behavior: It sleeps deep on the ocean floor to build its energy; it sleeps quietly.
social: Nothing is said about Kingdra together. A sleeper in uninhabited depths is presumably alone.
defense: Nothing is said about how Kingdra defends itself. At depths where nothing else survives, nothing threatens it.
habitat: Extreme ocean depths that are otherwise uninhabited: it sleeps on the seafloor, where no other life forms can survive, and lives in caves on the seafloor.

moves: It is strong despite its compact size. It can easily pick up and carry an adult human on its back.

dossier.summary: The young of Donphan: a small, very strong elephant with a long snout. For its nest Phanpy digs a vertical pit at a river's edge and marks the ground around it with its trunk to tell others the place is taken. In the quiet morning hours it comes ashore to shower with its trunk; when others gather they douse each other thoroughly, then dry off at the water's edge, and in the heat it fans itself with its big ears. It swings its snout around playfully and bumps with it to show affection, but it is so strong it can send you flying, and it can carry an adult on its back. In HeartGold it lives on Route 45 and Mt. Silver; in SoulSilver, Teddiursa has its place.
diet: Filed with Donphan as a plant-eater, from its body plan and its line; the machine reading's rock-eater comes from its Ground type alone.
senses: Odor Sleuth, a scenting move, is in its list; the entries say nothing of its senses.
behavior: During the deserted morning hours it comes ashore and deftly uses its trunk to take a shower.
social: When others gather around, they thoroughly douse each other with water.
defense: Its strength: its snout can send you flying.
habitat: River edges, where it digs its nest; it comes ashore, so it spends time in the water too. The Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is rough terrain.

dossier.summary: Donphan is a heavy, tusked herd animal of rough mountain country: 1.1 m tall but 120 kg, with a hide so tough that ordinary blows don't scratch it. It attacks by curling into a ball and rolling into its foe, and its charge is said to be able to knock down a house. Rank in the herd goes by tusk size, and tusks take a long time to grow. As Phanpy it is a riverbank youngster that nests in pits dug at the water's edge, showers with its trunk in the quiet morning hours and cools itself by fanning its ears. In Johto the line lives on Route 45, the mountain road below Blackthorn, but only in Silver, Crystal and HeartGold.
diet: Phanpy learns Natural Gift by level-up (Lv 19), a move that needs a held Berry, and has the Pickup ability; both hint that the line handles and collects food items, perhaps fruit.
senses: Phanpy learns Odor Sleuth at level 1, a sniffing move, which suggests the trunk is a nose in function as well as form.
behavior: Its favourite attack is to curl into a ball and charge, rolling at high speed; once rolling it can't easily stop.
social: Donphan lives in herds ranked by tusk size: the longer and bigger the tusks, the higher the rank.
defense: Armour: a hide so tough that a normal attack won't scratch it.
habitat: Gen 3 Pokédex habitat: rough terrain. The adult entries put it on mountain trails, where it clears rock and mud slides.

dossier.summary: Miltank is an all-female grassland Pokémon, and almost everything the Pokédex says about it concerns its milk. It gives over five gallons a day, sweet enough for children and nourishing enough to be called the ultimate drink for the sick or weary, and the milk grows richer after it has a calf or when babies are near. Nothing in canon says what it eats, how it lives with its own kind, or how a species with no males breeds. In Johto it grazes the same routes as Tauros, an all-male species of the same egg group, though no entry links the two.
diet: Its grassland habitat and cow-like build suggest a grazer, and its milk output implies it eats a great deal; neither is stated.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Detecting babies nearby, which changes its milk (241.7), implies it can sense young by sight, sound or smell, but the cue isn't named.
behavior: Activity pattern is unclear. Gold and Silver list it on Routes 38 and 39 in the morning, day and night alike; Crystal lists it only in the morning and day; HeartGold and SoulSilver don't split by time.
social: Its milk becomes richer when it is around babies, not only its own, which suggests it responds to any young nearby and could nurse young that aren't its own.
defense: Its level-up repertoire is heavy-bodied: Defense Curl (Lv 5) then Rollout (Lv 19), Stomp (Lv 8), Body Slam (Lv 24) and Gyro Ball (Lv 41). Read together, it curls and rolls into attackers or tramples them.

dossier.summary: The larva of the Tyranitar line, and the clearest life cycle in the Pokédex: it is born deep underground, eats the soil around it, and can't come up until it has eaten its way to the surface, where it sees its parents' faces for the first time. Once it has eaten enough to make a mountain it falls asleep and becomes a pupa, Pupitar. It is small but very heavy (0.6 m, 72.0 kg), a body of rock skin. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only on Mt. Silver, one in twenty encounters on most floors and one in ten at the top.
senses: It develops in darkness: it 'cannot see its parent's face' until it reaches the surface, so sight only matters once it is up.
behavior: Underground it eats; once it has eaten enough it falls asleep so that it can grow.
social: It has parents and meets them only at the surface: until it eats its way up it 'cannot see its parent's face' (Ruby and Sapphire) or 'its parents' faces' (Emerald).
defense: Nothing in the Pokédex describes how a Larvitar defends itself. Underground, under tonnes of soil, it is out of reach of most animals.
habitat: Mountains: born deep underground, and the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain.

abilities: The Pokémon may heal its own status problems.

defense: Its shell is as hard as sheet rock, and it is also very strong. Its THRASHING can topple a mountain.

dossier.summary: The pupa of the Tyranitar line, and a pupa that won't keep still. Pupitar's shell is as hard as sheet rock or bedrock, and inside it the animal already has arms and legs and can move freely. It makes a gas in its body, compresses it and blasts it out to launch itself like a jet or a rocket, and its body can hit solid steel without harm. Its thrashing can topple a mountain. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives only on Mt. Silver's third floor, one encounter in twenty.
diet: No entry says Pupitar eats. The line's entries put all the eating in the larva, which sleeps once it has eaten enough to make a mountain.
behavior: It will not stay still, even while it is a pupa.
defense: Armour: a shell as hard as bedrock that survives a collision with solid steel.
habitat: Mountains: the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is mountain, and its thrashing can topple one.

abilities: The Pokémon summons a sandstorm in battle.

about: Its body can't be harmed by any sort of attack, so it is very eager to make challenges against enemies.

dossier.summary: An armoured mountain giant with a life cycle like an insect's: larva, pupa, adult. Larvitar is born deep underground and eats soil until it has eaten its way to the surface and, as two Hoenn entries put it, can finally see its parents' faces; once it has eaten 'a large mountain' it sleeps and becomes Pupitar, a rock-hard pupa that still moves and can launch itself by venting gas. The adult brings down mountainsides to make its nest and roams the peaks looking for a fight; in a rampage it buries rivers, and maps must be redrawn. In Johto the young live on Mt. Silver.
diet: Larvitar eats soil, and keeps eating until it has eaten 'a large mountain'.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Larvitar's entries treat seeing its parents as the reward for reaching the surface, implying it develops in darkness and uses sight once out.
behavior: It seeks fights: it roams the mountains looking for new opponents, and, unable to be harmed, is eager to challenge them.

dossier.summary: Altaria is a light, cloud-winged dragon (1.1 m, 20.6 kg) that rides updrafts high into the sky and looks like a fluffy cloud in flight. It sings or hums in a clear soprano that leaves listeners feeling as if they are dreaming, and a beautiful melody heard deep in the mountains, far from people, is Altaria humming. It can also launch intensely hot fireballs, and an Altaria that bonds with a person wraps them in its soft wings and hums. It grows from Swablu, a tame, fastidiously clean little bird that sits on people's heads and whose flocks move closer to towns each spring after a hungry winter. In HeartGold and SoulSilver, Swablu appears only as a swarm on Route 45, the road below Blackthorn.

habitat: The sky: it flies, dances and wheels among white, billowing clouds.

dossier.summary: Milotic is a 6.2 m serpentine Pokémon of the bottoms of large lakes, famous above all for its looks: its scales shift through rainbow colours with the angle of view, and it has been painted and sculpted for generations. It develops from Feebas, a ragged, ignored, hardy fish that eats anything and schools in weedy ponds and rivers, and in Gen III–IV only a Feebas whose beauty has been raised becomes Milotic. No Milotic is wild in these games.

dossier.summary: Absol is a white, horned mountain quadruped (1.2 m, 47 kg) that senses subtle changes in the sky and the land and foretells natural disasters. It rarely comes down from its harsh, rugged mountains, and when it does appear before people it has come to warn them. Because disasters followed its appearances it was long mistaken for a bringer of doom, and a rumour that its horn senses disaster made it a target, so it fled deeper into the mountains. It lives a hundred years or more. In Johto it is not native: HeartGold and SoulSilver have it only through the Hoenn radio broadcast, which puts it in nearly every cave, including the Ice Path and the Dark Cave at Blackthorn.
diet: Its wild moves are mostly cutting and biting attacks (Slash, Night Slash, Psycho Cut, Bite, Pursuit), which suggests a predator, but that is a reading of moves.

defense: Its first defence is distance: it lives high in rugged mountains and, once hunted, fled deeper into them.
habitat: It lives in a harsh, rugged mountain environment and very rarely ventures down.

dossier.summary: The winged adult of the Bagon line, and the rival's SoulSilver Pokémon. Its whole line is a story about wanting to fly: Bagon throws itself off cliffs every day and grows a steel-hard head from the falls, Shelgon shuts itself in an iron shell while its cells rebuild its body, and Salamence is what grows when, after many long years, a sudden mutation gives it wings. It wheels across the sky spouting flame for joy, and when it is enraged it loses all thought and rampages out of control, scorching fields and mountains. It is never wild in a Gen I-IV game; in HeartGold and SoulSilver Bagon is only in the Johto Safari Zone.

dossier.summary: A small, very agile fire primate of craggy mountains: it scales sheer cliffs to live on their tops, and burns gas made in its own belly as a flame from its rear end. The fire is a sign of health, burning weakly when it feels sick, and rain can't put it out, but Chimchar puts it out itself before it sleeps, to prevent fires. Nothing says what it eats. It is the first stage of SoulSilver's Infernape, and in the Gen I-IV games it is only ever a starter gift in Sinnoh; no Johto game has one.

abilities: Powers up Fire-type moves in a pinch.

dossier.summary: A fast, fire-crowned primate of high crags that fights with all four limbs. The line starts as Chimchar, which climbs sheer cliffs to live on craggy mountaintops and burns gas made in its belly as a flame at its rear; that flame is a signal as well as a weapon, weakening when the animal is sick and, in Monferno, showing rank in the pack. Infernape carries its fire as a crown and on its hands and feet, and its fire never goes out. Nothing in the Pokédex says what any stage eats, and no game has it in the wild.
diet: Whatever it eats has to feed both the animal and a fire that never goes out, so its food needs are probably high for its size.
senses: Nothing is said about its senses. Reading rank from flame size and the brightness of a blue face pattern implies good colour vision in Monferno.
behavior: Extremely fast and agile: beaten by none in quickness, and it throws its enemies around.
social: Monferno lives in packs with ranks: a bigger tail fire and a brighter blue pattern on the face mean higher rank.
defense: Monferno manages distance with fire: it stretches its tail flame to look bigger and intimidate attackers, and controls the flame's intensity to keep foes at the range it wants.

dossier.summary: A small, proud penguin of northern shores. Piplup is a skilled swimmer that dives for over ten minutes to hunt, wears thick down against the cold, and walks so badly it often falls over, then puffs up its chest as if nothing happened. Its pride runs through every entry: it hates accepting food from people, doesn't like being looked after, and won't listen to its Trainer. It is the first stage of SoulSilver's Empoleon. In the Gen I-IV games it is only ever a Sinnoh starter; no Johto game has one.
diet: It dives for over 10 minutes to hunt.
behavior: A poor walker that often falls down, yet its strong pride makes it puff up its chest without a care.
social: Its pride is the social trait the entries return to: it doesn't like to be taken care of, and it won't listen to its Trainer.
defense: Nothing describes how it defends itself. Bide (Lv 22), which stores up damage and returns it, and Mist (Lv 36) are its defensive moves.

dossier.summary: The solitary middle stage of the Empoleon line. Every Prinplup believes it is the most important, so they can never form a group and each lives alone, away from the others. It searches for prey in icy seas, and its wings deliver blows that snap even the thickest trees. Between the proud, care-refusing chick and the adults that follow a leader, Prinplup is the loner stage. It is never wild in any Gen I-IV game.
diet: It searches for prey in icy seas.
social: It lives alone, away from others; apparently every one of them believes it is the most important.
defense: Its wing blows, strong enough to snap the thickest trees, are its defence as well as its weapon.
habitat: Icy seas, where it hunts; its young live along shores in northern countries (393.2).

dossier.summary: A large, proud diving bird of cold northern seas, with wing edges sharp enough to cut drifting ice. Empoleon swims as fast as a jet boat and carries three horns on its beak; the leader of a group has the biggest. habitat: Shores in northern countries, hunting in icy seas.

dossier.summary: A floating, magnetic Steel-and-Electric Pokémon that exists only because of where its parent was standing. Magnezone forms when a Magneton is exposed to a special magnetic field, which the HeartGold and SoulSilver Pokédex says changes its molecular structure; a group that tried to make it happen by scientific means failed. Its line feeds on electricity, hovers on electromagnetic waves, and in numbers disrupts radios, televisions and machinery, and Magneton is said to be three Magnemite linked by magnetism. Few animals in the Pokédex sit so far from ordinary biology: genderless, without egg moves, and impossible to evolve anywhere in Johto.

It is such a glider that, catching even a faint breeze properly, it could circle the globe without flapping once. dossier.summary: A huge, shaggy, ice-tusked survivor of an ice age. Mamoswine flourished worldwide while the ice lasted and declined as it melted; a frozen one dug out of 10,000-year-old ground is said to have woken up. Its young are Swinub, small rooting pigs with noses sensitive enough to find mushrooms, berries and even hot springs under ice, and they are common in the Ice Path, right beside Blackthorn. In between comes Piloswine, so shaggy it can't see, which finds its way by smell and sound and just keeps charging.
diet: Swinub roots for food by rubbing its snout on the ground; its favourite food is a mushroom that grows under dead or dried grass.
senses: Smell is the line's main sense: Swinub's nose is very sensitive and finds food and hot springs under ice; Piloswine, which can't see, checks its surroundings with its nose.
behavior: Swinub follows its nose: if it smells something enticing it dashes off headlong after it.
defense: Size, ice tusks and a charging habit: Piloswine charges repeatedly at whatever is in front of it, hackles up.
habitat: An ice-age animal: it flourished worldwide during the ice age and thinned out when the climate warmed and the ice dwindled.
